candidates.abstract: We develop the theory of the beta functions attached to the $\mathcal{R}(p,q)-$deformed quantum algebras of Hounkonnou and Bukweli Kyemba, for structure functions whose deformed numbers are generated by two deformation functions $φ_{1}>φ_{2}>0$. Working with the Jackson type series representation of the deformed integral, we define a first kind beta function on $[0,1]$ from the deformed power $(1\ominusφ_{2}t)^{y-1}$, extended to complex exponents, and a second kind beta function on the half line from $(1\oplusφ_{1}t)^{-x-y}$. The first kind function equals $φ_{1}^{(y-1)(2x+y-2)/2}Γ_{\mathcal{R}(p,q)}(x)Γ_{\mathcal{R}(p,q)}(y)/Γ_{\mathcal{R}(p,q)}(x+y)$ for all complex arguments with positive real parts; we derive its general shift identity, its exchange defect $φ_{1}^{(y-x)(x+y-1)/2}$, a commutative symmetrisation unique up to a constant, its asymptotics and a deformed Euler integral for a deformed Gauss hypergeometric function, which yields a deformed Gauss summation. candidates.title: Spatial switching near a four-loop homoclinic bouquet: a mechanism for multi-bump bound states in coupled nonlinear Schrödinger systems
candidates.abstract: We study how a localized standing wave of a coupled nonlinear Schrödinger (CNLS) system can switch between components from one pulse to the next. The standing wave reduction of the CNLS system yields a four-dimensional Hamiltonian system with two reflection symmetries, in which four elementary pulses correspond to a bouquet of homoclinic loops to a saddle. For saddle eigenvalues $\pmλ_{1},\pmλ_{2}$ satisfying $0<λ_{1} < λ_{2} < 2λ_1$, and under suitable nondegeneracy assumptions, we construct stable and unstable invariant manifolds of the four-loop bouquet. Apart from trajectories asymptotic to the saddle in the corresponding time direction, these manifolds characterize one-sided trapping near the bouquet within the critical Hamiltonian level, namely the level set containing the saddle equilibrium. Both manifolds have codimension one in this level. We prove that if they intersect transversely away from the bouquet, producing super-homoclinic orbits, then there exist infinitely many multi-bump homoclinic orbits to the saddle. These orbits correspond to multi-bump localized standing waves of the CNLS system.

candidates.title: Spectral characterizations of sub-Gaussian heat kernel bounds
candidates.abstract: Grigor'yan, Hu and Lau, in Conjecture 3.9 of [Springer Proc. Math. Stat. 88 (2014): 147--207], asked whether a Faber--Krahn inequality and matching bounds for the bottom of the Dirichlet spectrum on balls characterize sub-Gaussian heat kernel upper bounds. We give a counterexample on the Euclidean plane. Our counterexample uses a planar diffusion associated with a Dirichlet form from the work of Li and Sun in [Ann. Appl. Probab. 34 (2024), 4193--4236]. The bottom of the Dirichlet spectrum on every ball of radius $r$ is comparable to $r^{-2}$ meanwhile for balls centered on the $x_1$-axis, the mean exit time starting at the center is comparable to $r^3$ as $r\downarrow0$. This also shows that the exit-time hypotheses used to characterize heat kernel upper bounds in [Stochastic Process. Appl. 189 (2025): 104707] and [Math. Nachr. 299 (2026): 2566--2589] cannot be omitted. We then give a novel spectral characterization of heat kernel upper bounds in terms of the first Dirichlet eigenpair of balls. candidates.title: Online Statistical Inference for Derivative-Free Constrained Stochastic Optimization
candidates.abstract: We study statistical inference for nonlinear equality-constrained stochastic optimization problems in settings where derivative information is unavailable or expensive to obtain. While recent advances in stochastic sequential quadratic programming (SSQP) have enabled efficient online optimization, existing methods either rely on gradient information or suffer from high computational costs. To address these limitations, we develop a sketched derivative-free SSQP (SDF-SSQP) method that simultaneously achieves computational efficiency and valid statistical inference. By leveraging randomized sketching, the proposed method reduces the per-iteration computational cost to $O((d+m)^2)$, where $d$ is the dimension of the decision variable and $m$ is the number of constraints, making it well suited for large-scale problems. To overcome the challenges that both sketching and zeroth-order approximations introduce for statistical inference, we adopt a random-scaling approach that eliminates the need for explicit estimation of the asymptotic covariance matrix. candidates.title: Sampling at Scale: Distributed Multi-Agent Trajectory Optimization
candidates.abstract: Multi-agent trajectory optimization poses two coupled challenges: effectively exploring non-convex landscapes and scaling favorably to large teams of agents. Sampling-based methods are natural candidates for the exploration challenge but scale poorly with problem dimension. Moreover, their off-the-shelf integration into distributed optimization introduces a fundamental trade-off: sampling either fails to address the constraint-induced non-convexity or its search space grows with neighborhood size. We address this gap by introducing a $\underline{D}\text{istributed}$ $\underline{S}\text{ampling-based}$ $\underline{T}\text{rajectory}$ $\underline{O}\text{ptimization} \ \text{(DS-TO)}$ architecture built on a splitting mechanism tailored to sampling. Under this splitting, each agent samples only in its own control space, independent of neighborhood size, while still remaining exposed to both the constraint-induced non-convexity and the decisions of other agents. The resulting algorithm is fully decentralized, requiring only neighborhood communication, with all local updates executed in parallel across agents. candidates.title: Agent Evaluation Without Ground Truth: A Null Proportion Perspective
candidates.abstract: The correctness of actions taken by agents is typically evaluated against known, externally verified ground truth labels, such as whether a proof is correct or whether code compiles and passes unit tests. However, as coding and science agents are entrusted with more end-to-end autonomy -- proposing interventions, running experiments, and deciding what to deploy and investigate next -- whether an agent's actions genuinely improve an outcome must be inferred from noisy, often inconclusive experiments. To evaluate agents in this setting, we define agent quality as a weighted sum of correct decisions along its trajectory, using sequences of $e$-values as statistical evidence regarding correctness in place of ground-truth labels. Our framework accommodates arbitrarily dependent decisions, data-dependent trajectory termination, dynamically generated hypotheses, and quality measures defined after the trajectory concludes. We construct upper and lower bound estimators and confidence sets for agent quality with statistical guarantees that hold uniformly over agent trajectory distributions and establish instance-wise sharpness of our estimator class. candidates.title: Symbolic Proof Compression and Fractal Universality: A Conditional Non-Constructive Refutation of the Riemann Hypothesis
candidates.abstract: Building on S.~C.~Woon's (1994) fractal and symbolic reformulation of Voronin's Universality Theorem, we construct a formal, non-constructive proof-by-contradiction architecture exploring the Riemann Hypothesis ($\mathsf{RH}$). Woon's Corollary~3 permits arbitrary finite binary strings to be encoded into nowhere-vanishing exponential waveforms on a closed disk inside the critical strip. Combining effective upper bounds for Voronin universality (Good, Garunkštis) with Cauchy-integral Taylor decoding yields an explicit finite rational grid $\mathcal{G}_{L_0}$ below an effective ceiling $H_{\mathrm{crit}}(L_0)$ within which every formal proof of bit-length at most $L_0$ is imprinted with zero flipped digits. We introduce a conjectural \emph{Zeta-Universal Symbolic Proof Compression Hypothesis} ($\mathsf{SPC}_{\mathsf{RH}}$), positing that the global regularity implied by $\mathsf{RH}$ compresses true $Π_1^0$ statements about $ζ(s)$ into $\mathsf{ZFC}$ derivations of bounded length $L_0$. Assuming classical logic and $\mathsf{SPC}_{\mathsf{RH}}$, Gödel--Carnap diagonalization over bounded zeta-encoded provability yields a contradiction. candidates.title: From the ELBO to Maximum Likelihood: Convergence of Variational Autoencoders for Nonlinear Mixed-Effects Modeling
candidates.abstract: Nonlinear mixed-effects (NLME) models are the central statistical models of pharmacometrics, where they support dose selection, individualized dosing and regulatory decisions in drug development. Statistically, NLME modeling is a marginalized likelihood problem. Variational autoencoders (VAEs) solve such problems with a neural network encoder that amortizes the approximation of the intractable posterior distribution, and allow the integration of AI components into NLME modeling. This paper provides the convergence analysis of the VAE-NLME algorithm. First, its version for the evidence lower bound (ELBO) is proven to converge almost surely to the set of stationary points of the ELBO, without assuming that the encoder is trained exactly. Second, the final VAE-NLME algorithm trains the encoder on the ELBO by gradient-based optimization and uses it as proposal for importance-weighted sufficient statistics. It converges almost surely to the set of stationary points of the marginal log-likelihood, without any assumption on the training of the encoder. Thus, it combines the fast gradient-based training of VAEs with the limit of maximum likelihood estimation.

candidates.title: Monadicity of noncommutative measurable spaces over $C^{\ast}$-algebras
candidates.abstract: In a recent paper, Tobias Fritz and the second author identified $σC^*$-algebras as a tentative noncommutative analogue of measurable spaces. We advance this analogy by establishing monadicity of $σC^*$-algebras over $C^*$-algebras and proving several results of interest to both the category theory and operator algebra communities. In detail, we show that: - The associated probabilistic morphisms, $σ$-cpu maps, admit a description via a comonad closely related to the Giry monad. Equivalently, $σ$-cpu maps can be characterized by a universal property. - The category of $σC^*$-algebras and $σ$-homomorphisms is locally $\aleph_1$-presentable. - $σC^*$-algebras have a tensor product induced by the maximal tensor product of $C^*$-algebras and satisfying an analogous universal property. - The notion of CP-instruments, defined as $σ$-additive assignments from a $σ$-algebra to a space of completely positive maps, can be adapted to this setting by taking as target the set of $σ$-normal completely positive maps between $σC^*$-algebras. This yields a bijective correspondence with $σ$-cpu maps out of the tensor product of the previous item.

candidates.title: Breaking Resonance: Square-root acceleration for Metropolis-adjusted randomized Hamiltonian Monte Carlo
candidates.comment: 40 pages, 5 figures. Lean 4 formalization of the main results at https://github.com/nawafbourabee/breaking-resonance-lean (doi:10.5281/zenodo.24483261)
candidates.abstract: Hamiltonian Monte Carlo with a fixed integration time can fail to mix because of resonances, and randomizing the integration time removes them. We prove that Metropolis-adjusted HMC with velocity Verlet and random integration times mixes from a warm start in a number of transitions that does not depend on the condition number, for every integration-time law satisfying a Fourier condition that we call non-resonant; uniform, exponential and triangular laws are examples. For a target density proportional to $e^{-U}$ on $\mathbb R^d$, where $U$ is $m$-strongly convex with $L$-Lipschitz gradient and $L_H$-Lipschitz Hessian and $κ=L/m$, the number of gradient evaluations needed to reach a fixed total variation accuracy is, up to constants and logarithmic factors, $\sqrt{κd}+\sqrt{L_H}\,(d/m)^{3/4}$. This is the first square-root condition-number bound for this sampler beyond Gaussian targets. The proof converts relative-entropy contraction of the unadjusted proposal into a conductance bound for the adjusted chain, and shows that the integration-time law enters only through its characteristic function. candidates.title: Alpha-Beta Pruning via Monadic Continuations
candidates.abstract: Alpha-beta pruning is a fundamental technique in game-playing AI, enabling efficient minimax search by avoiding the exploration of branches that cannot affect the optimal decision. We present a monadic formulation of alpha-beta pruning based on the combination of the continuation monad and the reader monad. Unlike previous approaches that encode alpha-beta bounds into the types of available moves, our construction records these bounds within monadic outcomes, leaving the move types unchanged. We further show that the ordinary continuation monad suffices to compute not only optimal outcomes but also optimal plays, by extending the outcome type to include the corresponding sequences of moves. This provides an alternative to generalisations of the continuation monad proposed to address the inefficiencies associated with the selection monad in alpha-beta search. We illustrate our approach with an implementation of Tic-Tac-Toe, observing a 39-fold reduction in the number of plays evaluated, compared with exhaustive search, in computing an optimal play. candidates.title: Synchronized Memory-Dependent Intracellular Oscillations for a Cell-Bulk ODE-PDE Model in $\mathbb{R}^3$
candidates.abstract: We develop a hybrid asymptotic-numerical theory for a cell-bulk ODE-PDE model in $\mathbb{R}^3$ to analyze the long-range diffusive coupling of spatially localized, dynamically active cells. In the limit of small cell radius $\varepsilon\ll 1$, we derive a novel integro-differential ODE system for the intracellular dynamics, in which the 3-D bulk diffusion field is effectively replaced by a time-memory kernel whose strength depends on the inter-cell distances. To compute long-time solutions efficiently, we implement a fast time-marching scheme for this integro-differential system that is inspired by the \emph{sum-of-exponentials} method. This scheme is applied to Sel'kov intracellular kinetics, which is a conceptual two-component model for a conditional oscillator. Our analysis reveals that, in contrast to the more strongly coupled 2-D case, each cell in $\mathbb{R}^3$ experiences only a weak $\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon)$ coupling effect from the other cells in the population. Consequently, individual cells that exhibit oscillatory intracellular dynamics can only synchronize over very long time scales of order $\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon^{-1})$ when they are separated by $\mathcal{O}(1)$

candidates.title: Beyond Classical Minimax Rates: Quantum Sampling in Gradient-Based Simulation Optimization
candidates.abstract: We study gradient-based search for a class of convex simulation optimization problems with gradients estimated from noisy outputs. With independent outputs, the optimal classical convergence rate for the expected objective gap is of order $O(N^{-2/3})$, where $N$ is the query budget. We apply quantum mean estimation to paired finite differences and progressively increase their estimation accuracy as the perturbations shrink, improving the convergence rate to $O(N^{-4/3})$. Furthermore, we show that coupling nearby evaluations improves the classical and quantum convergence rates to $O(N^{-2/(3-κ)})$ and $O(N^{-4/(3-κ)})$, respectively, where $κ\in[0,1]$ describes the variance reduction in paired outputs. Thus, quantum estimation halves the accuracy exponent in query complexity across coupling orders. Moreover, we establish matching lower bounds and show that these accuracy exponents are minimax optimal for fixed decision dimension, even when query locations and batch sizes are adaptive. Reconstruction from feasible differences retains the exponents when every simulation query must be feasible and accommodates boundary optima.

candidates.title: The Generalized Volterra Signature
candidates.abstract: In this paper, we introduce the generalized Volterra signature \(\gvsig(\bX)\) of a path \(\bX\), extending the classical Volterra signature introduced in [Hager, Harang, Pelizzari \& Tindel, arXiv:2603.04525, 2026], which extends Lyons' path signature to the Volterra setting. We establish a new algebraic structure to encode the generalized Volterra signature. We also establish a generalized Chen's identity. By restricting the differential trees to ladder trees, we introduce the geometric Volterra signature \(\geovsig(\bX)\) and establish the shuffle product of its signature components. To the best of our knowledge, the shuffle product for the Volterra signature is the first of its kind and allows us to formulate a universal approximation theorem for geometric Volterra signatures. For a special class of kernel functions, we prove the existence of an extended path \(\Bar{\bX}\) and relate its classical signature to the geometric Volterra signature of the original path \(\bX\).

candidates.title: Blow-up size for the noncommutative rank of linear symbolic matrices with low-rank coefficients
candidates.abstract: The noncommutative rank (nc-rank) of a linear symbolic matrix $A = A_0 x_0 + A_1 x_1 + \dots + A_m x_m$ is the supremum of $1/k$ times the rank of the $k$-th blow-up $\sum_i A_i \otimes X_i$ of $A$, where $X_i$ are $k \times k$ matrices consisting of distinct variables. In this paper, we show that the blow-up size needed to attain the nc-rank is bounded by the ranks of the coefficient matrices. More precisely, if $A_1, \dots, A_m$ have rank at most $r$, with no restriction on $A_0$, then the $k$-th blow-up attains the nc-rank for every $k \geq r$. This holds for rectangular matrices over an arbitrary field, and unifies and extends the known results that $k = 1$ suffices for rank-one coefficients (Lovász, 1989; Ivanyos, Karpinski, and Saxena, 2010) and that $k = 2$ suffices for skew-symmetric coefficients of rank two (Oki and Soma, 2025). We present two applications. First, if $r$ is a constant, then the nc-rank of an $n \times n$ linear symbolic matrix can be computed by a randomized algorithm with $O(m n^2 + n^ω)$ arithmetic operations over a sufficiently large field, where $ω$ is the matrix multiplication exponent. candidates.title: A new angle on matrix-vector complexity
candidates.abstract: The theory of worst-case matrix-vector complexity has been useful for guiding the design of fast linear algebra algorithms. However, there is a large theory-practice gap in the study of *one-sided* methods, which use matrix-vector products with $\mathbf{A}$ but not $\mathbf{A}^\top$. In practice, for fundamental problems like solving linear systems, one-sided methods like GMRES are often the fastest. By contrast, worst-case analysis often shows pessimistic results, for instance showing that one-sided methods cannot solve a linear system with ideal condition number 1 unless they read the whole matrix $\mathbf{A}$. Such worst-case complexity results do not reflect real-world experience. To address this issue, this paper proposes a different theory of worst-case matrix-vector complexity that includes information on the positioning of the eigenvalues of $\mathbf{A}$ *in the complex plane*. Specifically, we characterize the "well-behavedness" of a matrix $\mathbf{A}$ through its *spectral condition number* $κ$ and its *angular eigenvalue gap $θ$*, the angle of the largest sector not containing an eigenvalue. candidates.title: A Spectral Zoo of Genus-Zero Free Boundary Minimal Surfaces with Many Boundary Components
candidates.abstract: We study critical points of the length-normalized first Steklov eigenvalue $\barσ_1$ on genus-zero surfaces with $b$ boundary components. By a theorem of Fraser and Schoen, their first eigenfunctions give free boundary minimal surfaces in the unit ball. After uniformization, the domain is the round sphere minus $b$ round caps, with a weight on the boundary circles. A layer potential formulation gives the eigenvalues, their derivatives and a certificate for each critical point, and an exact multipole system for the caps. We compute a spectral zoo of 268 numerically certified critical points with up to $b=2252$ boundary components, including the $27$ embedded examples listed by Schulz. With their symmetry groups and Morse indices, the critical points satisfy a signed count for $3\le b\le10$. Most belong to families built from rings of boundary components. As the rings fill in, these appear to converge to the free curve minimal surfaces of Karpukhin and Noutchegueme, unions of flat disks and catenoidal annuli that meet along circles on the sphere. candidates.title: Linear programming certificates for dimension bounds of hyperbolic Coxeter polytopes
candidates.abstract: We use linear programming to derive upper bounds for the dimension of hyperbolic Coxeter polytopes from local geometric and arithmetic estimates. Rational certificates give the bounds $57$ for finite-volume polytopes, $17$ for compact polytopes, and $15$ for compact arithmetic polytopes. In the finite-volume case, the certificate is a weight function on incidences between vertices and two-dimensional faces. In the compact cases, the inequalities concern squared norms of orthogonal projections of a fixed tangent vector at a vertex farthest from an interior point. We give a common formulation of these linear programs, prove monotonicity in the dimension threshold, and describe the exact verification of the certificates. The local estimates are taken from the companion geometric proofs.

candidates.title: Spectral Summation and Critical Asymptotics of Newton Knot Invariants
candidates.abstract: The symmetric colored invariants of a knot are defined at integer colors, and Newton interpolation assembles them into a formal function of a continuous color variable. We sum it by $q$-Borel--Laplace summation and use the resulting analytic function to study the invariants as $q\to1$. For every knot and every rank, the critical summation level is a rational number determined by the growth of the colored invariants; when it is positive, the critical Borel transform is meromorphic in the whole plane. When the Newton coefficients have analytic tails, the Borel transform is assembled from convergent sums of simple poles along geometric progressions, and for such sums the Stokes jump of the Laplace sum determines every pole and residue. For an infinite family of twist knots containing the figure-eight knot, a positive Markov kernel gives an exact formula for the remainder of the Newton series. With it we show that, near a root of the Alexander polynomial, the rescaled analytic interpolation converges to Gaussian and Scorer-type profiles, uniformly for complex values of the rescaled color, and we determine how fast the rank may grow before these limits change. candidates.title: An Order-Optimal Square-Root Bound for Online Maximin Share Allocation with Known Types
candidates.abstract: An allocator knows the indivisible goods, the number $n$ of agents, and the $k$ possible additive valuations. Each agent reveals their type on arrival and must immediately receive an irrevocable bundle. Kulkarni, Mehta, and Shahkar established a deterministic guarantee of $1/k$ of maximin share (MMS) and an upper bound of $2/(\sqrt{k}-2)$ for $k>4$. We determine the optimal order $Θ(k^{-1/2})$ by constructing a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm, Single-or-Select. On every arrival sequence, it gives each agent a fraction $(1/\sqrt{2}-o(1))/\sqrt{k}$ of their truncated proportional share. This share dominates MMS and is the largest target $y$ for which the item values capped at $y$ sum to at least $ny$. By specializing the construction of Kulkarni et al. to two arrivals and counting its types exactly, we sharpen the upper bound to $(\sqrt{2}+o(1))/\sqrt{k}$ even for binary valuations. For two arrivals with binary valuations and every $k\ge2$, the optimal fraction is $1/p$, where $p$ is the largest integer with $1+\binom{2p}{2}\le k$. candidates.title: Heights and energies of polarized fibrations of varieties II. Fibrations over a polarized base
candidates.abstract: We extend the height and energy inequalities for fibrations over curves to a fibration $f:X\to Y$ over a polarized variety $(Y,B)$. For an integrable relatively nef adelic line bundle $\bar L$, we prove a height inequality under the assumption that $L$ is nef on the inverse image of a geometric generic complete-intersection curve in $Y$. We deduce a lower bound for the local energy at almost every complex or nonarchimedean realization of a fixed polarized model when $L$ is $f$-ample. For a slope semistable bundle on a fixed polarized complex variety, we show that the infimum of the energy on its projective bundle equals the infimum of Donaldson's functional on Hermitian quotient metrics, with the normalization given below.

candidates.title: Exact Collision Gradients for Ellipsoids in Differentiable Simulation
candidates.abstract: Differentiable simulation enables gradient-based optimization in learning and control problems involving collisions, but its gradients are least reliable at the moment of impact, when the velocities jump. A fixed-step simulator detects a collision only after the bodies overlap, and some differentiable simulators correct for this with a linear estimate of the time of impact. In this paper, we study impacts between ellipsoids. We show that the gradient error of this estimate grows with the obliqueness of the collision, the curvature at contact, and the time step, and that ignoring spin adds a further error. Subsequently, we find the time of impact with continuous collision detection on the Perram Wertheim contact function and differentiate through the touching condition rather than the search. This gives exact gradients at any step size. We demonstrate our method on an optimal control problem and a system identification problem. In both, exact gradients recover the optimal control and the true parameters, while the linear estimate does not, even when it accounts for spin.

candidates.title: A Kernel Framework for Linear Operator Equations
candidates.abstract: Solving linear operator equations with nonlocal terms or heterogeneous constraints often requires specific numerical schemes. We develop a unified approach based on embedding such equations into a reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS). Differential, boundary, and integral operators are represented by their Riesz representers in the RKHS. The equations are solved in the regularized least-squares sense at finitely many collocation points. The solution is a finite linear combination of operator-induced representers and is obtained from a single linear system. Its sensitivities, such as financial Greeks, follow by direct differentiation. To reduce the computational cost for large collocation sets, we introduce a Nyström approximation based on subsampling the operator-induced representers. It yields the best approximation of this solution within the reduced trial space, in a regularized empirical norm. Numerical examples cover ordinary, partial, and partial integro-differential equations, including multi-asset and jump-diffusion option pricing.

candidates.title: Uncertainty Quantification and Global Sensitivity Analysis of Patient-Specific Coronary Hemodynamics Under Unsteady Flow Conditions
candidates.abstract: Patient-specific computational models of the coronary arteries demonstrate transformative potential for physiological assessment, identifying hemodynamic markers associated with disease progression, and optimizing treatment. Unfortunately, these models rarely account for input parameter uncertainty, limiting confidence in predictions and their clinical interpretation. Herein, we present a novel uncertainty quantification-finite element framework that integrates computationally efficient techniques to characterize and propagate uncertainty through patient-specific coronary simulations under unsteady flow conditions. Principal component analysis characterized variability in pulsatile coronary velocity waveforms, while uncertainty in blood pressure, viscosity, density, and heart rate is represented through probability distributions. Polynomial chaos expansion (PCE) enabled efficient uncertainty propagation and global sensitivity analysis across three patient-specific models, quantifying variability in time-averaged wall shear stress (WSS), oscillatory shear index, and cross-flow index. candidates.title: Smale's Mean Values And Geometric Mean Values
candidates.abstract: We prove that, for every integer $d>2$ and every $L>0$, there exists a polynomial of degree $d$ whose geometric mean value exceeds $L$. This result demonstrates that the geometric mean value alone is insufficient to establish the smallest upper bound for the minimum of Smale's mean values. Under certain additional assumptions, we derive upper bounds for the geometric mean value, thereby verifying Smale's mean value conjecture for several subclasses of polynomials. Furthermore, we connect Smale's mean values to Fekete points. Motivated by this connection, we formulate a new problem concerning Fekete points in the spirit of Smale's mean values.

candidates.title: An equivariant index theorem for the Heisenberg calculus
candidates.abstract: We derive a local fixed-point formula for the equivariant index of Heisenberg elliptic operators on closed contact manifolds equipped with an action of a compact Lie group preserving the contact form. The formula expresses the character of the equivariant index in terms of a cyclic-cohomological character of the noncommutative Heisenberg principal symbol. The main new ingredient is the construction of traces, one on each fixed-point set, defined by integration over twisted conjugacy classes in the Heisenberg group. The proof proceeds by a K-theoretic reduction to the equivariant index theorem of our paper "Toeplitz operators on contact manifolds and equivariant K-homology".

candidates.title: SOTS: Signature-based Optimal Transport Selection
candidates.abstract: Training data selection for machine learning models is a critical bottleneck in industrial applications where expert annotation is costly and time-consuming. Existing coreset selection methods for time series either ignore temporal structure entirely or cannot handle variable-length, irregularly sampled, multi-channel signals, the setting most common in industrial monitoring and testing. We introduce SOTS (Signature-based Optimal Transport Selection), an unsupervised coreset selection framework for irregular multivariate time series (IMTS) classification. Each sample is mapped to a truncated path signature, capturing the joint geometric structure of its channels, and the coreset is selected by greedily minimizing the Sliced Wasserstein distance between the empirical signature distributions of the candidate subset and the full dataset, a criterion for which we establish a convergence guarantee for random coresets. We validate SOTS on a real-world, highly imbalanced industrial I&C testing dataset, where SOTS-Greedy exceeds 95% of full-dataset accuracy using only 30% of the training data, outperforming standard coreset baselines at most budgets. This advantage generalizes to public UE

candidates.title: Airy Path Integral Representation for the Kadomtsev-Petviashvili Equation
candidates.abstract: We give a representation for solutions of the Kadomtsev-Petviashvili II (KP-II) equation as path integrals over the Airy line ensemble. The initial condition enters directly as a potential, bypassing the usual direct and inverse scattering constructions. We establish the representation for broad classes of signed initial data, prove uniqueness in specified solution classes, and derive a restart identity expressing solutions as Airy path integrals of their own earlier states. For arbitrary real $L^2$ initial data, a centered version of the Airy occupation represents the standard global KP-II flow. We show how the representation recovers the classical Marchenko determinant for Korteweg-de Vries (KdV), and identify a Brownian-path amplitude with the classical KP-II heat-scattering coefficient. We obtain explicit formulas for soliton solutions and derive KP from a Toda equation for nonintersecting Brownian bridges. Finally, we use the restart identity to characterize one-point distributions of the KPZ fixed point through their singular initial conditions, and derive sharp lower-tail asymptotics directly from KP.

candidates.title: Transformers with Signatures: Towards Universal In-Context Learning in Path Space
candidates.abstract: In-context learning (ICL) enables transformers to adapt to new tasks from demonstrations without updating their parameters. However, theoretical guarantees for transformers remain limited in general, and elusive in particular when target responses depend nonlinearly on the evolution of observed paths. We establish an ICL framework for path space, using path signature features. Building on the universal linear approximation property of signatures, we construct explicitly a causal softmax transformer with two attention heads per layer that emulates in-context Lasso. Under sparse signature approximation and suitable moment and concentration conditions, we establish finite-sample prediction error bounds. Our analysis goes beyond the IID data setting in the existing ICL theory, allowing dependence among demonstrations and the query. Experiments on in-context sparse recovery, nonlinear path regression, execution-cost prediction, and financial payoff inference demonstrate robustness to changes in observation grids and adaptation to unseen market environments. candidates.title: Admissibility of Linear Time Series Models under Cone Constraints
candidates.abstract: Time series analysis extends beyond vector-valued observations to evolving probability densities, quantile functions, and covariance operators. These objects carry intrinsic constraints, raising questions about the admissibility of additive linear models, which have long served as a foundation for time series modelling and theory. We give a necessary and sufficient support condition for a stationary Hilbert-space linear process to remain in a closed convex cone almost surely. Innovations with unbounded lower tails, including Gaussian innovations, confine randomness to the cone's largest linear subspace. For fractional filters with convergent normalized cumulative coefficients, the leading stochastic directions obey the same restriction, even with bounded innovations. For real-line quantiles, variation under unbounded lower tails and leading fractional accumulation can occur only through location shifts. For cone-valued processes, partial sums of centred stationary increments remain bounded in mean square when evaluated by any linear functional that is nonnegative on the cone, in contrast to the growing variance of a random walk. We derive an exact slope criterion for locally absolu

candidates.title: A direct majorant and an improved Huber constant on cofinite Fuchsian groups
candidates.abstract: To obtain an effective upper bound for Huber's constant on cofinite Fuchsian groups, we introduce an algorithm that bypasses the quantitative Karamata Tauberian theorem in estimating spectral-counting growth by direct use of re-optimized Gaussian kernel instead. Further steps involve the different choice of a compactly supported test function, keeping linear and constant terms in the spectral estimate, optimizing the exact cusp geometry, and retaining the full explicit primitive-geodesic majorant in subsequent Chebyshev estimates. The more direct path is established to control the difference between the size of the hyperbolic term in the Selberg trace formula and the second Chebyshev function. Finally, the self-improvement device combined with a knowledge of low-lying spectral data leads to the sharpening that in the case of $\mathrm{PSL}(2,\mathbb{Z})$ reads $C_{\mathrm{Hub},\mathrm{PSL}(2,\mathbb{Z}) }<199$. The improvement factor is greater than $8.3\cdot10^{10}$ compared to what was claimed by the initial algorithm and greater than $1.1\cdot10^6$ compared to the currently known bound.

candidates.title: A Sylow reduction for isomorphisms of Cayley graphs on abelian groups of cube-free order
candidates.abstract: The isomorphism problem for Cayley graphs is one of the fundamental problems in algebraic combinatorics. Dobson studied this isomorphism problem and asked whether, assuming that the group generated by the left regular representation and its conjugate under an isomorphism admits a complete sequence of normal block systems, the isomorphism problem for Cayley digraphs on a finite abelian group of cube-free order can be reduced to the corresponding problem on its Sylow subgroups. We answer this question affirmatively. We first prove that color-preserving isomorphisms preserving the fiber partition on direct products $A\times H$ of abelian groups of coprime orders, where $|H|$ is a prime or the square of a prime, have a product decomposition property. Applying this property successively to the Sylow subgroups of a cube-free-order abelian group $G$, we show that if two colored binary Cayley structures on $G$ are connected by a color-preserving isomorphism $f$ for which $\langle G_L,f^{-1}G_Lf\rangle$ admits a complete sequence of block systems, then they are also connected by a color-preserving Sylow coordinate isomorphism. This yields the corresponding Sylow reduction for solving sets.

candidates.title: A characterization of almost everywhere convergence of subsequences of Walsh--Fourier partial sums
candidates.abstract: We characterize the increasing sequences $(ν_j)$ in the set of positive integers $\mathbb N$ along which the Walsh--Fourier partial sums $s_{ν_j}(f)$ of every integrable function $f$ converge almost everywhere to $f$. This resolves a problem that Konyagin posed in his invited address at the 2006 International Congress of Mathematicians~\cite{K06}. The criterion concerns the binary expansions of the integers $ν_j$. Divide each $ν_j$ by $2^k$. Convergence holds if and only if, for some $K\in\mathbb N$, the number of distinct positive quotients whose remainder has binary variation larger than $K$ is bounded independently of the scale $k$. This is also equivalent to the weak type $(1,1)$ inequality for $\sup_{j\in\mathbb N}|s_{ν_j}(f)|$, and if the criterion fails, then the partial sums of some integrable function along $(ν_j)$ are unbounded at every point. The criterion contains the bounded variation condition and Konyagin's condition for separated spectra, and we give examples, for convergence and for divergence, that are not covered by the earlier results.

candidates.title: Alexander modules and Milnor fibers of topological line arrangements
candidates.abstract: We study the Alexander module and a distinguished cyclic cover, which we call the \textit{topological Milnor fiber}, of the complements of topological line arrangements. For every topologically realizable combinatorial type with $n \geq 2$ lines, where $n$ is not a prime power, we prove that the first Betti numbers of its topological Milnor fibers are unbounded. Moreover, any finite abelian group occurs as a direct summand of the integral homology of a topological Milnor fiber within the given combinatorial type. As an application, we show that every topologically realizable combinatorial type with $n \geq 2$ lines admits a realization whose complement has no $2$-dimensional CW model.

candidates.title: Fractional minimality of the Simons cone for $s$ close to $1$
candidates.abstract: We prove that the Simons cone in $\mathbb R^8$ minimizes the fractional perimeter $P_s$, under compact perturbations, whenever $s$ is sufficiently close to $1$.

candidates.title: Hadwigerś Covering Conjecture in Three Dimensions
candidates.abstract: Let $K \subset \R^3$ be an arbitrary convex body, that is, a compact convex subset of $\R^3$ with nonempty interior. We prove unconditionally that $K$ can be covered by eight smaller positive homothetic copies of itself: there exist a scalar $λ\in (0, 1)$ and translation vectors $v_1, \dots, v_8 \in \R^3$ such that \[ K \subseteq \bigcup_{i=1}^{8} (λK + v_i). \] This resolves Hadwiger's covering conjecture in three dimensions. The proof works in Boltyanski's equivalent boundary illumination formulation and is completely self-contained. Parallelepipeds are covered directly by eight translates of $\frac{2}{3} K$. For any convex body $K$ that is not a parallelepiped, we place its centrally symmetric halved difference body $S = \frac{1}{2}(K - K)$ in John's position ($B^3 \subseteq S$) and show that the spherical average of its support function satisfies $8 \int_{S^2} h_S \, d\sigmatilde < 12$, with equality only for orthogonal cubes. Using outer polyhedral approximations together with Cauchy's planar perimeter formula, the full spherical measure of directions not parallel to any boundary segment of $K$, and lower semicontinuity of curve variation, we find a unit vector $w_* \in S^2$ w

candidates.title: A note on slicing
candidates.abstract: We give a short proof of Bourgain's slicing theorem with the explicit bound $L_K\leq\sqrt{5/π}$ for every convex body $K$. The argument combines the strong thin-shell inequality obtained from the moment-measure method of Chen and Klartag with an entropy estimate along Eldan's stochastic localization. The proof uses neither $M$-ellipsoid theory nor the reverse Santaló inequality.

candidates.title: Semi-Implicit Finite Volume Central Scheme for Hyperbolic Systems of Balance Laws with Adjustable Free Parameter approximation to relaxed source term
candidates.abstract: This study develops a generalized framework for constructing a three-stage predictor-corrector finite volume scheme for solving hyperbolic balance laws with stiff relaxation source terms. The proposed scheme extends the central Nessyahu-Tadmor (NT) framework for the nonhomogeneous part of PDE and the integrals of the source terms are computed using an undetermined coefficient approach to introduce a free parameter \(α\), which offers flexibility in formulation. A unified theoretical analysis is then carried out to characterize the properties of the resulting scheme and determine the admissible range of \(α\). Specifically, uniform consistency and asymptotic properties are investigated along with $A$ -stability and $L$-stability, with the corresponding theoretical constraints combined to establish a common admissible range for the free parameter. The numerical performance of the scheme is subsequently evaluated through a sequence of test problems. Smooth-solution tests are used to assess its accuracy, while one-dimensional benchmark problems arising from different mathematical models are considered to examine its performance in comparison with existing numerical schemes. The assessm

candidates.title: Quasiperiodicity breakdown and homoclinic bifurcations in the forced librations of a parametric oscillator
candidates.abstract: Above its instability threshold, a parametrically excited oscillator settles into one of two phase states. The response of these states to a second, much slower modulation of the same stiffness is investigated. In the rotating frame, this modulation periodically varies the detuning and drives the phase librations. When the modulation is slow compared with the libration frequency, the phase states follow adiabatically. As the two frequencies become comparable, this approximation breaks down and the driven libration resonates with the intrinsic one. This nonadiabatic regime is examined for a Duffing oscillator with nonlinear damping. The averaged equations describe a periodically perturbed planar system with integrable unperturbed dynamics, whose homoclinic loop is derived in closed form. The phase states persist as invariant tori supporting quasiperiodic motion. Their stability and period-doubling bifurcations are captured by a damped Mathieu equation, in which the modulation contributes to both parametric stiffness and parametric damping. A Melnikov analysis yields explicit thresholds for separatrix splitting and the onset of homoclinic intersections, which are corroborated by nume

candidates.title: Simultaneous Waring problems for binary forms and the geometry of rational curves
candidates.abstract: We investigate the simultaneous Waring problem for binary forms and its geometric applications to rational curves. By analyzing the minimal free resolution of the simultaneous annihilator, we establish formulas for both simultaneous Waring ranks and border Waring ranks including explicit computations for binary monomials. As a geometric application, we explicitly describe parametrizations of rational curves up to projective equivalence. We determine the minimum dimension of a rational normal scroll containing the curve as a section of its ruling in terms of the minimal generators of the corresponding simultaneous annihilator. For rational curves lying as divisors on rational normal surface scrolls, we characterize their smoothness and describe the generators of their defining ideals.

candidates.title: Hochschild operations and other invariants of stable equivalences of Morita type
candidates.abstract: We study stable equivalences defined by bimodule tensor identities over a commutative ring $R$. For the $R$-split exact structure, these identities preserve positive Hochschild homology and positive Hochschild cohomology with its cup product, Gerstenhaber bracket and, in prime characteristic, restricted power. A triangular comparison also identifies the relative singular Hochschild cochain complexes as $B_\infty$-algebras. For reduced pairs of finite-dimensional Frobenius algebras over an algebraically closed field, with diagonalizable Nakayama automorphisms, we construct compatible Frobenius functionals and compare the Tate--Hochschild BV operators in all degrees. For flat algebras over $R$ we give a Hochschild-cohomological criterion for comparing marked associative deformations. It applies to biadjoint Morita-type pairs and, by reduction, to all stable equivalences of Morita type between finite-dimensional algebras over any field. We compare the Bezrukavnikov--Ginzburg maps in characteristic zero by using a common triangular deformation or by lifting a two-sided tilting complex. We also compare marked module deformations over local Artin rings and their augmented universal rings

candidates.title: Rotationally symmetric fractional minimal surfaces
candidates.abstract: In this paper, we provide a non-trivial example of an $s$-minimal surface that is invariant under rotations. More precisely, we study alternating radial sets whose boundaries are finite or locally finite unions of concentric spheres and prove that, fixing the outer radius to $r=1$, there exists a radial configuration for which the fractional mean curvature $H_s$ vanishes at every free interface. We then show that rescaling radial maximizers by their innermost radius and passing to the limit yields a properly embedded, rotationally symmetric, locally finite hypersurface satisfying $H_s=0$ at every point of the boundary.

candidates.title: A sharp polygonal Finsler-Hadwiger inequality
candidates.abstract: For every simple $n$-gon of area $A$ with side lengths $a_1,\ldots,a_n$, we prove \[ \sum_{i=1}^n a_i^2 \ge 4\tan\fracπ{n}\,A +c_n\sum_{i<j}(a_i-a_j)^2, \qquad c_n=1-\frac{\tan(π/n)}{\tan(π/(n-1))}, \] with the convention $c_3=1$, so that the case $n=3$ is exactly the Finsler-Hadwiger inequality. The coefficient $c_n$ cannot be improved, and equality holds only for regular polygons. The extremal configurations are far from the regular $n$-gon: the constant is approached by cyclic polygons in which one side shrinks to zero while the others become the sides of a regular $(n-1)$-gon (a doubled segment when $n=3$). The proof combines the classical fact that cyclic polygons maximize area for given side lengths with a two variable minimization using the half central angles. We also compute the larger optimal coefficient for nearly regular polygons, and show that the best constant in the joint stability estimate for side lengths and vertex radii grows like $n^2$.

candidates.title: Relaxation dynamics of Winfree oscillators on Riemannian manifolds
candidates.abstract: We study exponential relaxation to equilibrium for Winfree-type models on Riemannian manifolds. For the sphere model with entrainment point $p$ and canonical influence, we derive convergence to equilibrium, whenever no oscillator starts at the antipode $-p$. For the corresponding canonical model on $\mathrm U(d)$, we obtain the same convergence whenever no initial matrix has the eigenvalue $-1$. Both results hold above explicit coupling thresholds depending on the initial configuration and the frequency matrices. For a broader class of unitary influence functions, the same spectral condition yields exponential convergence for sufficiently large coupling strengths. Finite-time entrance into positively invariant stable regions and contraction estimates yield exponential convergence rates and equilibrium uniqueness within those regions. A finite symmetry construction on Lie groups realizes the unitary model and a special unitary analogue as invariant Kuramoto--Lohe subsystems, yielding local relaxation results. Finally, we formulate an abstract Winfree model on Riemannian manifolds and establish local exponential relaxation in a fixed coordinate neighborhood under quantitative attract

candidates.title: Poisson Statistics for Values of Binary Quadratic Forms in Short Intervals
candidates.abstract: We study the number of integers represented by a binary quadratic form in short intervals. Extending the work of Freiberg, Kurlberg, and Rosenzweig on sums of two squares, we formulate an analogue of the Hardy--Littlewood prime $k$-tuple conjecture for the integers represented by a genus of primitive positive definite binary quadratic forms of a fixed negative discriminant. We show that this hypothesis implies that the number of integers represented by a genus, and by each class in the genus, in a random interval $(n,n+y]$ with $n\le x$, where $y$ is $τ$ times the average spacing $\sqrt{\log x}/b(d)$, is asymptotically Poisson distributed with parameter $τ$. The proof uses the method of moments, with Bernays' asymptotic for the number of represented integers in place of the prime number theorem, and an adaptation of Ford's simplified argument for the average of the singular series. We also give numerical evidence for the hypothesis.

candidates.title: Group classification of a class of systems of nonlinear diffusion equations. I
candidates.comment: Revised and corrected version of the article published in Ukr. Math. J. 78, 40 (2026). In particular, the group classification of the first subclass has been corrected and substantially refined
candidates.abstract: We study the Lie symmetries of a class of systems of (1 + 1)-dimensional nonlinear diffusion equations. The equivalence algebra and the kernel of the maximal Lie invariance algebras of this class are found. We prove that there exist exactly nine inequivalent subclasses of this class for which the corresponding diffusion systems admit Lie symmetry extensions. We also carry out the exhaustive group classification of the systems of nonlinear diffusion equations from the first subclass.

candidates.title: Exact transport exponents for random mosaic operators
candidates.abstract: We determine the exponentially time-averaged transport exponents of period-two random mosaic operators, with zero potential on the even sites and iid potential on the odd sites. For every bounded, strictly positive, nonconstant single-site law, on one event of probability one, $β_f^-(q)=β_f^+(q)=\max\{0,2/3-ν_H(f)/(3q)\}$ for all nonzero finitely supported states $f$ and all $q>0$. The positive odd integer $ν_H(f)$ is determined by divisibility by $H$ and cancellation against the bounded zero-energy solution. In particular, the large-moment exponent is $2/3$ for every such state, while point sources on the two sublattices have second-moment growth powers $1$ and $1/3$. We obtain matching resolvent bounds by retaining the vanishing orders of two polynomial source channels through the singular normalization at zero energy. We also prove deterministic lower bounds for every bounded positive configuration. No density assumption is imposed on the law.

candidates.title: Contractible 4-Manifolds with Nonnegative Ricci Curvature and Euclidean Volume Growth
candidates.abstract: We prove that every contractible smooth 4-manifold admitting a complete Riemannian metric with nonnegative Ricci curvature and Euclidean volume growth is homeomorphic to $\mathbb{R}^4$. More precisely, every compact subset lies in the interior of a connected compact regular domain with simply connected complement. The key construction produces compact domains whose boundaries admit positive scalar curvature and which are regular sublevels of global strictly three-convex Morse exhaustions. A topological criterion forces the exterior fundamental group to be trivial whenever it contains no nonabelian free subgroup and satisfies the resulting boundary, homological, and relative cell hypotheses; in the geometric application, this group is finite. Its proof uses a cellular formulation of the Gerstenhaber-Rothaus theorem and a smooth filling obstruction. The resulting complements give simple connectivity at infinity, and Freedman's recognition theorem completes the argument.

candidates.title: Chern classes of vanishing cycles for maps having no blowups
candidates.abstract: We study the nearby and vanishing cycles for maps with no blowups. For holomorphic maps between complex manifolds admitting at most ICIS, we show that the Riemann-Hurwitz defect in Chern classes is compensated for by the Chern class transformation of the Milnor number constructible function.

candidates.title: KKT Atlas: Learning Low-Dimensional Local Scenario Models for Contextual Stochastic Optimization
candidates.abstract: In contextual stochastic optimization, integrated learning trains conditional models on operational loss, but repeatedly solving stochastic programs with many scenarios is costly. We propose KKT Atlas, which partitions contexts into local charts and identifies a low-dimensional subspace per chart from decision gradients of the scenario cost. It generates shared scenarios by jointly fitting subspace coordinates and context-dependent probabilities. We show that one more scenario than the subspace dimension suffices to approximate the conditional Karush-Kuhn-Tucker optimality condition under regularity conditions, yielding decision and risk bounds under local strong convexity, with generalization error scaling with the compact parameter dimension. On three synthetic problems, Atlas uses 4-18 scenarios per decision versus 500 for direct-solve full-support integrated learning. It attains comparable or lower risk with about $4$-$23\times$ construction and $13$-$61\times$ batch deployment speedups. Atlas also achieves lower risk than clustering-based reduction at matched support budgets. In real-world European grid reserve commitment, Atlas compresses 728 scenarios to 8-9, cutting constru

candidates.title: Strong convergence rate for non-autonomous slow-fast SDEs driven by Brownian motions and α-stable processes
candidates.abstract: In this paper, we establish a quantitative strong averaging principle for a class of time quasi-periodic slow-fast stochastic differential equations driven by both Brownian motions and multiplicative $α$-stable Lévy processes. We show that the slow component converges strongly to an autonomous averaged equation with rate $\varepsilon^{\min\{1-1/α_2,\,1/(ν+2)\}}$, where $α_2\in(1,2)$ is the fast stability index and $ν$ comes from the quasi-periodic structure. Our strategy is as follows. We first derive the intermediate step of the averaging principle to average out the effect of fast-variable oscillations on the system, although the averaged variable still depends on $\varepsilon$. We obtain the convergence rate $\varepsilon^{1-1/α_2}$. Furthermore, under the uniformly quasi-periodic conditions, we show that the slow component converges strongly to the solution of some autonomous averaged equation, whose coefficients independent of $\varepsilon$. We thus obtain the convergence rate $\varepsilon^{1/(ν+2)}$. candidates.title: An extended Matsumoto--Yor property for free GIG distributions
candidates.abstract: We prove a two-parameter extension of the Matsumoto--Yor property for free generalized inverse Gaussian distributions. The transformation is the reciprocal form of a known matrix Yang--Baxter map. Our proof combines the independence-preserving property for matrix generalized inverse Gaussian distributions with asymptotic freeness. Since the relevant spectra stay in compact subsets of the positive half-line, continuous functional calculus and polynomial approximation suffice to handle all inverses. The same argument yields the free Matsumoto--Yor property itself for all positive rates of the free Poisson law, including those for which this law has an atom at zero. We also discuss the limit in which one of the two parameters tends to zero: the limiting laws are free Poisson only when the rate is at least one, so for smaller rates this limit does not recover the free Matsumoto--Yor property.

candidates.title: The Anatomy of Piecewise-Linear Learned Indexes
candidates.comment: 14 pages, 4 figures, 4 tables; core theorems machine-checked in Lean 4
candidates.abstract: Piecewise-linear approximation (PLA) learned indexes (PGM-index, FITing-Tree, RadixSpline, PLEX, PLIN) compress sorted keys into $\pm\varepsilon$ segments, yet prior theory stops at coarse $Θ(\varepsilon^2)$ single-segment bounds. At the bottom layer, optimal greedy PLA covers $κ_{\rm opt}\varepsilon^2/v_0 \approx 3.54\,\varepsilon^2/v_0$ keys per segment on independent gaps and $κ_{\rm opt}\varepsilon^2$ under any smooth density ($v_0=1$), while anchored and chord fitters retain $Θ(\varepsilon^2/v_0)$ coverage. Across recursive layers, a law-of-large-numbers heuristic--invoked to claim $O(\log\log n)$ height for the PGM-index--suggests summing $Θ(\varepsilon^2)$ gaps averages out fluctuations. We prove this fails under Endpoint Promotion (EP): stopping-time fluctuations reset relative gap variance at every depth, locking fanout at $C_\varepsilon \approx 19.861\,\varepsilon^2$, expected height at $\log n/\log C_\varepsilon + O(1)$, and lookup at $Θ(\log n)$. To break this barrier, Rank-Equispaced Promotion (RE) samples pivots at equal rank strides. Each stride sums a fixed number of base gaps, so relative variance decays across layers and cumulative coverage squares at each step. E

candidates.title: The polygonal Steklov--Weinstock inequality
candidates.comment: 74 pages. Ancillary files contain the verification code, coefficient tables, and recorded certificate outputs
candidates.abstract: We prove that for every integer $N \ge 3$, the regular $N$-gon uniquely maximizes the scale-invariant first positive Steklov eigenvalue $L(P)σ_1(P)$ among all simple planar polygons $P$ of positive area with at most $N$ sides, up to similarity (and up to congruence at prescribed perimeter). Our proof combines two complementary realizations of the Rayleigh--Ritz variational principle. For convex competitors, we transplant a first Steklov eigenfunction of the regular reference polygon: for triangles, affine transplantation aligned with a longest side yields both the sharp inequality and a two-sided linear stability bound in terms of the maximal side-length deviation; for convex $N$-gons with $N \ge 4$, a piecewise harmonic fan transplantation across radial sectors matches traces along the internal seams. In the quadrilateral case, centering the fan at the vertex average pairs opposite sides and controls the displacement of the diagonal midpoints, whereas for $N=5$ the spectral deficit dominates both the area deficit and the squared vertex and Hausdorff distances to the regular pentagon. candidates.title: Aalen-Johansen as an augmented IPCW estimator
candidates.abstract: We show that, in every sample, the widely used Aalen-Johansen estimator of a state occupation probability is an inverse probability of censoring weighted estimator augmented by a working Markov prediction from each subject's current state. This identity explains the robustness of the Aalen-Johansen against departures from the Markov assumption. It also reveals that its influence function differs from the semiparametric efficient one by two orthogonal components: the information in earlier history beyond the current state, and the error of the Markov prediction. Based on this decomposition, we propose a practical, model-free least-squares augmentation of the Aalen-Johansen that regresses the outcome on a history score, narrowing the gap under non-Markov processes without increasing the asymptotic variance. Its advantages are validated both theoretically and in simulations.

candidates.title: Elastic rebound in viscous fluid: an efficient rigid--elastic splitting with an asymptotic gap model
candidates.abstract: We formulate and test a model for an elastic body that falls under gravity onto the bottom of a container filled with a viscous incompressible fluid and rebounds without topological contact. The body is a rigid body plus a small, quasi-static elastic deformation, represented by a fixed compliance operator. In the near-contact patch, the thin fluid film is described by a Reynolds equation with cavitation. This allows the use of coarse meshes that need not resolve the gap, enabling efficient simulation. The film is coupled implicitly to the elastic surface displacement and to the rigid normal motion. The bulk fluid is coupled monolithically to the rigid body. For the axisymmetric case with vertical translation, the coupled step reduces exactly to a small dense nonlinear problem for the film pressure, with the bulk eliminated through a $2x2$ affine map. The model is implemented in NGSolve and compared with the experiments of Hagemeier et al. (2021) and the Eulerian FSI simulations of Wahl et al. (2021a). For a PTFE ball the approach agrees with the Eulerian FSI to 1\%. For a soft rubber ball (St $\approx 120$) the purely elastic model gives about three times the measured rebound. Mate

candidates.title: Finite rank and compactness of finite sums of Toeplitz products on the harmonic Bergman space
candidates.abstract: We completely characterize finite rank and compactness for finite sums of products of Toeplitz operators on the harmonic Bergman space of the unit disk, assuming boundedness only of the full harmonic symbols. Reflecting the appropriate symbols reduces sums of Toeplitz products and small Hankel products to Toeplitz product sums. For sums of mixed Toeplitz and small Hankel products in either order, right multiplication by a fixed unitary reflection gives the corresponding reduction. These reductions preserve rank and compactness. Finite rank is characterized by symbol identities and a cubic divisibility condition on the coefficient polynomials obtained after choosing bases over one-variable rational function fields. We also obtain an exact rank formula. Compactness is characterized by boundary vanishing of the diagonal symbol sum and uniform decay of the centered symbol tensor on hyperbolic disks of fixed radius as their centers approach the boundary. For a sum of $N\ge1$ products, an equivalent compactness criterion uses weighted derivatives of the symbol components up to order $N$. When $N$ is even, the conditions of order $N$ cannot be omitted.
