candidates.title: Mass gap for finite connections in supercritical percolation
candidates.comment: 270 pages with thirteen figures. This paper supersedes arXiv:2408.16636 incorporating much of its content into Part I. The earlier preprint may be consulted for a freestanding proof of a stretched-exponential bound on renewal-block height
candidates.abstract: We consider finite open clusters based at the origin in Bernoulli bond percolation on $\mathbb{Z}^d$ for $d\geq3$ at a supercritical value $p>p_c(d)$, whose maximal height in the direction of a unit vector $\pmb{\ell}$ lies in a fixed-width window at distance $u$. Conditioned on this event, we prove that, except with probability exponentially small in $u$, such a cluster is populated at positive density by renewal points. Here, a renewal point $w$ is the only vertex of the cluster in the fixed-width band immediately below the height hyperplane through $w$. The main technical estimate is that, under this conditioning, the absence of a renewal point is exponentially unlikely. From it we derive an exponential mass gap for the irreducible pieces delimited by successive renewal points, and from the mass gap the stated renewal abundance. The mass gap, together with the renewal decomposition and endpoint estimates established here, yields a sharp point-to-point Ornstein--Zernike asymptotic for finite connectivity, with its Gaussian-type power-law correction. The multiplicative prefactor in this asymptotic is positive and real-analytic, and the associated equidecay and Wulff boundaries are

candidates.title: Finiteness and completeness of $g$-fans for real-weighted quivers
candidates.abstract: We study finiteness and completeness of $g$-fans for quivers with positive real weights. We characterize finite Coxeter type by the condition that every weight in the mutation class has the form $2\cos(π/m)$ for some integer $m\geq3$. Under total sign-coherence, we then show that a quiver with finitely many $g$-clusters is $2$-finite, that is, every weight in its mutation class is less than $2$. This also gives a new proof that $g$-finiteness implies finite Coxeter type. Assuming in addition that, for every initial quiver in the mutation class, each $c$-vector on a coordinate axis is a signed standard basis vector, we prove that the $g$-fan is complete if and only if there are finitely many $g$-clusters. The main geometric result states that the coordinate projection of every $g$-cone is contained in a $g$-cone of the corresponding full subquiver. Consequently, completeness and density pass to full subquivers.

candidates.title: Saddle-focus to saddle transition of 4D heteroclinic orbits resembling oscillatory and regularized shock waves of some dissipative Boussinesq systems
candidates.abstract: Oscillatory and regularized shock waves have long been studied to understand the formation and dynamics of undular bores in shallow waters, phenomena that typically arise from the interplay between dispersion, nonlinearity, and dissipation. In this work, we investigate and describe the nature and shape of traveling wave solutions that resemble oscillatory and regularized shock waves of some Boussinesq-type water wave models known as Bona--Smith systems in the presence of dissipation. The associated traveling wave equations are solutions of four-dimensional dynamical systems, leading to both computational challenges and rich structural behavior. In particular, to describe the properties of these traveling waves, we analyze heteroclinic orbits that connect two distinct equilibria, one of which undergoes a transition in the four-dimensional phase space from a saddle-focus to a saddle point as the dissipation parameter increases. This transition governs the nature of the wave profile, which evolves smoothly from an oscillatory shock wave to a regularized (non-oscillatory) shock wave. To compute such solutions, we introduce a finite-difference-based numerical method tailored for this cl

candidates.title: Eisenstein Cohomology and Critical Values of Certain \(L\)-Functions: A Root-Theoretic Combinatorial Lemma
candidates.abstract: This paper gives a root-theoretic extension of the Harder--Raghuram combinatorial lemma, relating criticality of adjacent $L-$values to degrees in nilradical cohomology, to maximal parabolics $P=MU$ of connected split reductive groups with irreducible, essentially tempered cohomological inducing data. At real places, the paper classifies the maximal parabolics for which the two Kostant degrees in the boundary comparison can agree at a regular shift. For each such parabolic, an admissible shift makes both adjacent arguments critical in every Langlands--Shahidi grade exactly when both Kostant degrees equal $\dim U/2$. The classification recovers the two-block parabolics of type $A$ with even product of block sizes (Harder--Raghuram, proved by Weselmann) and the isotropic-line parabolic of type $D_{2m+1}$ for $m\ge2$ (Bhagwat--Raghuram). The only exceptional cases are $P_1$ and $P_6$ of type $E_6$. In all other cases, roots of $U$ fixed by the longest Levi Weyl element confine simultaneous criticality to a singular wall, generalizing the odd-block obstruction for $\mathrm{GL}_N$. Their number is the difference of the fundamental ranks of $M$ and $G$. When the Kostant degrees differ, a

candidates.title: Turnpike Estimates and Limiting Behavior for $N$-Player Differential Games under Displacement Monotonicity
candidates.abstract: We study the long-time behavior of open-loop Nash equilibria of $N$-player stochastic differential games with nondegenerate idiosyncratic noise, under displacement monotonicity of the costs and joint strong convexity of the Lagrangians. We prove an exponential turnpike estimate: as the remaining horizon grows, the decoupling fields of the finite-horizon Pontryagin systems converge exponentially fast to the solution of a stationary Pontryagin system, which is unique in a natural stability class, and on bounded time intervals the equilibrium states and controls converge to those generated by this solution. The limiting control is a strong open-loop equilibrium of an associated ergodic $N$-player game, and the ergodic constant $λ^{i,N}$ of each player is the same at every such equilibrium. For the finite-horizon game, the law of the equilibrium state, at times away from the initial and terminal times, is exponentially close in the Wasserstein distance $W_2$ to the invariant measure of the limiting dynamics. Finally, the equilibrium cost of player $i$ on $[t,T]$ equals $(T-t)λ^{i,N}$ plus a uniquely determined corrector, up to an error exponentially small in $T-t$.

candidates.title: A General Framework for Identifying the Joint Potential Outcome Distribution through Support Restrictions
candidates.abstract: Many causal estimands depend on the joint distribution of potential outcomes, which is generally not identifiable because only one potential outcome can be observed for each unit. To obtain identification, researchers often impose assumptions such as monotonicity and exclusion restriction that constrain the support of this joint distribution. For treatments and outcomes that each take finitely many values, we define a similarity matrix whose entries count, for each pair of potential outcome strata, the number of treatments yielding the same outcome. We then prove that, under unconfoundedness, identification holds if and only if this matrix is invertible, yielding a criterion directly verifiable from the support. In addition, we derive an identification formula for the joint distribution under these support restrictions and show that an average causal estimand is identifiable if and only if its integrand admits an additive representation on the restricted support. Finally, we derive sharp testable implications of the support restriction. Our results unify and generalize a broad range of identification results in the literature.

candidates.title: Infinite lower triangular matrices that are similar to their inverses but are not products of two involutions
candidates.abstract: Let $F$ be a field, and let $\GL_{\cf}(F)$ be the group of invertible column-finite matrices over $F$ indexed by $\bbN\times\bbN$. Denote by $\LT(F)$ (resp.\ $\UT(F)$) the subgroup consisting of lower (resp.\ upper) triangular matrices whose diagonal entries are equal to $1$. Every matrix in $\UT(F)$ is a product of two involutions. We show that, if $F$ has at least four elements, then $\LT(F)$ contains a matrix which is conjugate to its inverse by an invertible lower triangular matrix, but is not a product of two involutions in $\GL_{\cf}(F)$. The matrices can be chosen to be $4$-periodic. This gives a negative answer to a conjecture of de Seguins Pazzis.

candidates.title: Modular Schur functions and Macdonald characters
candidates.abstract: Modular Schur functions arose from the problem of determining the characters of simple polynomial representations of the general linear group in positive characteristic. We prove three results about these functions. (i) In finitely many variables, we obtain two bases for a space of symmetric polynomials with bounded degree in each variable, one consisting of modular Schur polynomials and the other of products of truncated complete symmetric polynomials. (ii) We determine the signs of the nonzero Schur coefficients of modular Schur functions, show that their absolute values are at most the factorial of the block weight, and characterize equality. (iii) Over an infinite field of prime characteristic, a modular Schur polynomial is a simple polynomial character exactly when its indexing partition satisfies the Carter condition, provided the number of variables is at least the degree. Thus we prove three conjectures formulated by Walker (1994). We also use the Heisenberg operators from the Schur coefficient calculation to prove positivity for Macdonald characters. After centering the Macdonald parameters at one and negating the auxiliary variables, the normalized power-sum matrix entrie

candidates.title: Schubert positivity for filtered bundles
candidates.abstract: We characterize formal filtered nefness of a formal quotient flag on a polarized Hodge--Lefschetz module by the formal nefness of its positive-rank total quotients. Using this criterion, we prove that quotient Schubert functors preserve formal nefness and that Schubert incidence modules inherit every commuting formally filtered nef flag. As geometric and numerical consequences, we recover the positivity criteria of Fulton--Lazarsfeld and Fulton and extend the Lorentzian polynomial theorem of Lu and Zheng to derived Schubert classes of filtered bundles. In combinatorics, our framework applies to tautological flags of flag matroids on ordinary and augmented matroid Chow rings as well as on the intersection cohomology of rational projective fans equipped with a common weight map. We deduce concordance-sensitive intersection inequalities, establish the Schubert positivity of the leading Riemann--Roch Chow class of a flag matroid, and show that the nonvanishing supports of derived Schubert numbers on an augmented Chow ring form the Higgs lifts of an intrinsically determined matroid quotient.

candidates.title: Upwind finite element approximation of the gradient blow-up time for a viscous Hamilton--Jacobi equation
candidates.abstract: We analyze an upwind finite element method with piecewise linear elements for a viscous Hamilton--Jacobi equation with a superquadratic gradient source term, subject to homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions. On polytopal inner approximations of smooth bounded domains in dimensions $N=1,2,3$, we prove maximum-norm convergence of the numerical solution to the exact solution before gradient blow-up and convergence of gradient-threshold times to the blow-up time under explicit mesh and regularity assumptions. We also verify the regularity assumption and finite-time gradient blow-up for an example on the disk, to which the main theorem therefore applies. Numerical experiments illustrate this gradient blow-up.

candidates.title: On the computation of Green's function in layered elastic media
candidates.abstract: We develop a recursive scheme for the computation of Green's function for time-harmonic elastic wave in three-dimensional layered media, based on a matrix basis representation in the Fourier domain and a classic interface reaction-transmission theory. With transversal rotational symmetry preserved, the scheme decouples the Green's function into SH waves and P-SV waves using five scalar functions, which are recursively solved at linear cost with respect to the number of total layers, regardless of the layers the source and target particles locate in. The resulting scheme leads to a stable numerical method ready for Hankel transform evaluation in the spatial domain, constituting a foundation for the analysis and efficient numerical simulation of elastic wave scattering in layered media.

candidates.title: Fractional Triangular Maximal Operators on Locally Finite Trees
candidates.abstract: We introduce and study the centered and uncentered fractional triangular maximal operators, $\mathcal{N}^γ$ and $\widetilde{\mathcal{N}}^γ$, on locally finite trees. A key geometric tool that consists of a family of overlapping triangles with total measure comparable to a ball is established, which facilitates the analysis of ball-type maximal operators. Our main results include: complete pointwise comparisons among these and classical fractional maximal operators on homogeneous trees; sufficient geometric conditions and counterexamples for general trees; and sharp $\ell^p \to \ell^q$ boundedness theorems for the new maximal operators, with optimal ranges of exponents verified by counterexamples. Finally, we compare the unboundedness regions of the ball-type maximal operator $\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^γ$ and the triangular maximal operator $\widetilde{\mathcal{N}}^γ$ on a prototypical tree, proving that the former's region strictly contains the latter's for all $0 < γ\leq 1$.

candidates.title: Analytic properties of distributions associated with multi-state Random Number Generators
candidates.abstract: We analyze the analytic properties of probability distributions associated with possibly unfair, multi-state Random Number Generators (i.e., dice). Specifically, given a $q$-sided die, if $x_i\in \{0,\ldots, q-1\}$ denotes the outcome of the $i^{\text{th}}$ toss, then $F(x)=\mathbb{P}[X\leq x]$ is the associated cumulative distribution function---a probabilistic generalization of the famed Cantor function. We first establish easily computable bounds for the $L^1$-distance between the possibly unfair $F$ and the uniform distribution $y=x$. We then show that $F$ is both upper- and lower-Hölder continuous, where the associated Hölder exponents are shown to be sharp. Finally, we establish recursive formulae for the moments, $\mathbb{E}[X^n]$, associated with $F$ and use these moments to provide sequences of step-functions that converge uniformly to $F$ from above and below.

candidates.title: Viscosity Solutions of Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman Integro-Differential Equations with Non-Lipschitz Running Costs
candidates.abstract: We study a class of parabolic Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman (HJB) integro-differential equations arising from stochastic recursive control problems with jumps. These equations involve a Lévy-type operator and an additional nonlocal term in the running cost. The underlying backward generator satisfies a monotonicity condition with polynomial growth in the backward variable and is uniformly continuous, but not necessarily Lipschitz continuous, in the state, Brownian, jump and control variables. We establish well-posedness, comparison and stability results for the corresponding backward stochastic differential equations with jumps, and derive a dynamic programming principle for the associated recursive control problem. Using approximation arguments and the stability of viscosity solutions, we show that the value function provides a viscosity solution of the HJB integro-differential equation. We further establish a comparison principle for bounded sub- and supersolutions and uniqueness within a prescribed growth class, under an additional uniform bound on the jump amplitudes.

candidates.title: Weighted Inequalities for the Fractional Maximal Operator on Trees with Flow Measures
candidates.abstract: This paper develops a weighted theory for the fractional Hardy-Littlewood maximal operator $M_{μ,γ}$, $0<γ<1$, on infinite trees equipped with flow measures. Such measures are typically nondoubling and exhibit exponential volume growth, so the classical Muckenhoupt theory does not apply directly. By replacing Euclidean balls with admissible trapezoids, a class of fractional $A(p,q)(μ)$ weights is introduced, and a Muckenhoupt-type theorem is established: for $1\le p<1/γ$ and $1/p-1/q=γ$, the operator $M_{μ,γ}$ is bounded from $\ell^p_μ(ω^p)$ to $\ell^q_μ(ω^q)$ if and only if $ω\in A(p,q)(μ)$. The endpoint case $p=1$ is characterized via a weak-type estimate.

candidates.title: Fibered-knot braids and symplectic fake quadrics
candidates.abstract: We construct aspherical symplectic four-manifolds with the rational cohomology ring of $S^2\times S^2$ by summing ruled surfaces along braided multisections. For each $m\geq1$, we form two symplectic sums with the same gluing map in the chosen surface markings and normal framings, using a stabilized braid for the trefoil in one sum and for the torus knot $T(2,7)$ in the other. Both sums have integral first homology $({\mathbb Z}/2)^2\oplus{\mathbb Z}/(4m)$. Their fundamental groups admit respectively $36$ and $24$ epimorphisms onto $S_3$, so the sums are nonhomeomorphic. We also vary the gluing while keeping the multisections fixed. In each of five product, twisted, and hybrid cases, this gives an infinite sequence in which the first homology groups have strictly increasing finite orders. All but finitely many members of each sequence admit no complex structure.

candidates.title: Sharp inequalities for fractional spherical maximal operators on finite graphs
candidates.abstract: This paper presents a systematic study of (quasi-)norm bounds for the fractional spherical maximal operator $M_{α,G}^{\circ}$ on finite connected graphs $G$. We establish sharp estimates for the operator norm of $M_{α,G}^{\circ}$ from $\ell^p(G)$ to $\ell^q(G)$ for $0 < p \leq q \leq \infty$, with explicit extremal values attained by complete graphs $K_n$ and star graphs $S_n$. We solve the corresponding extremal graph problem by showing that complete and star graphs are the unique maximizers of the operator norm in different parameter regimes. Additionally, we characterize graphs containing a universal vertex in terms of their operator norm. Finally, we analyze the spherical maximal operator $M^{\circ}_{G}$ on paths $P_n$, uncovering a clear divergence in the operator's behavior between odd and even lengths.

candidates.title: The Borel Topos
candidates.abstract: We construct a topos for Borel mathematics: statements which are true in Borel mathemaics correspond in a precise way to statements which are true in the internal logic of this topos. We investigate several other properties of this topos, including proving that it satisfies a Borel analogue of the Church-Turing thesis: the statement that every function on a standard Borel space is Borel. We also show that an earlier construction of a similar "Borel topos" by van Osdol does not suit these purposes because of an error in that paper.

candidates.title: Linear rank-\(k\) nonincreasing and preserving maps
candidates.abstract: We characterize the linear maps between rectangular matrix spaces that carry matrices of rank at most \(k\) to matrices of rank at most \(k\). Over every field, such a map has the form \(X\mapsto MXN\) or \(X\mapsto MX\T N\), or its entire image has upper rank at most \(k\). The proof uses polynomial functions on determinantal loci and extends Loewy's infinite-field theorem to all finite fields. Over fields with more than two elements, exact preservation of rank \(k\) implies rank-\(k\) nonincrease. Over \(\F_2\), for each \(k\ge2\), we construct a rank-\(k\) preserver that sends a rank-one matrix to a matrix of rank \(k+1\). For maps whose images have upper rank \(k\), three block rank equalities characterize exact preservation. Over \(\C\), we combine the Huang--Landsberg classification with a degree obstruction on \(\mathrm{PGL}_k\) to show that every primitive core of upper rank four arising from a rank-four preserver is, up to equivalence and transposition, a projected exterior-product space on \(\C^5\). If either source dimension exceeds five, every complex rank-four preserver is standard with full-rank factors or is a compression. A \(4\times5\) example attains the bound. Th

candidates.title: A short proof of Serre positivity
candidates.abstract: Recently, OpenAI found a proof of the positivity of Serre's intersection multiplicity. The two main ingredients are a descent result on rational $K$-theory with support; and a construction of certain category of asymptotic complexes that identifies with the category of perfect complexes over a connective (non-commutative) derived ring. In this article, we present a simpler proof of Serre positivity that circumvents the second step; instead, we use a ``reduction to the diagonal" trick via the $A_{\text{inf}}$-construction.

candidates.title: Normal edge-transitive bi-Cayley graphs of prime valency over nonabelian simple groups
candidates.abstract: Let $Γ$ be a connected graph of prime valency admitting a nonabelian simple group $R$ that acts semiregularly on the vertices with exactly two orbits. We prove that if the normalizer of $R$ in $Aut(Γ)$ is edge-transitive, then $Γ$ is bipartite and $R$ is characteristic in $Aut(Γ)$. We derive consequences for Cayley graphs and a criterion for semisymmetry. As an application, we construct bi-Cayley graphs over $A_p$ from the conjugates of a $3$-cycle under a cyclic group of order $p$, where $p>5$ is prime. These graphs are semisymmetric precisely when the support of the $3$-cycle is not a three-term arithmetic progression in $\mathbb{F}_p$.

candidates.title: Asymptotic Normality of the Pearson Correlation between Two Weakly Dependent Random Fields
candidates.abstract: We study the asymptotic behavior of the sample Pearson correlation coefficient between two weakly dependent random fields on a lattice of any fixed dimension. Under strict stationarity, $(BL,θ)$-weak dependence and mild moment conditions, we establish the consistency and asymptotic normality of the estimator on regularly growing domains, which need not be rectangular, with an asymptotic variance expressed through joint fourth-order moments. When the correlation is zero, asymptotic normality holds under weaker conditions. When the fields are independent, the asymptotic variance simplifies to a sum over spatial lags of products of their autocorrelations. The variance approximations behind the classic modified $t$-test, although derived for independent Gaussian fields, target the right variance even without Gaussianity. We also give sufficient conditions for asymptotic normality that are easy to check and cover bounded, Gaussian, $m$-dependent and independent fields. For Gaussian fields, summable auto- and cross-covariances suffice. These conditions rely on new closure results. Squares and products, although not Lipschitz, preserve $(BL,θ)$-dependence for Gaussian fields, and products

candidates.title: Verified two-sided bounds for the inf-sup constant of the divergence on planar polygons
candidates.abstract: The inf-sup constant $β(Ω)$ of the divergence governs the stability of the Stokes problem. For polygons, analytic lower bounds are far from the true value, and numerical methods either bound $β$ from above or require spectral-gap and mesh-fineness hypotheses that cannot presently be checked. We propose a method that produces verified lower bounds without any such hypothesis. It rests on the Friedrichs formulation of $β$ in the Bergman space and on a multiplier identity that controls the non-compact corner contribution pointwise, with the sharp corner constant; the remaining compact part is bounded by a finite matrix inequality that is checked in exact and ball arithmetic. We prove that the bounds converge to $β$. Together with enclosed Rayleigh quotients of explicit trial functions (and, for the square, the bottom $\frac12-\frac1π$ of the essential spectrum) this yields two-sided enclosures, e.g.\ $0.426245\leβ\le0.426252$ for the square and $0.303973\leβ\le0.304078$ for the L-shaped domain. candidates.title: Sharp Hellinger Risk of the Multivariate Gaussian NPMLE
candidates.abstract: For multivariate Gaussian location mixtures whose mixing distributions have coordinatewise sub-Gaussian tails, we prove that the unconstrained nonparametric maximum likelihood estimator attains the minimax rate $(\log n)^d/n$ under squared Hellinger loss. This holds for every fixed dimension $d\geq2$ and every fixed tail parameter $σ>0$. The upper bound applies to every measurable choice of a global likelihood maximizer and improves the earlier bound of order $(\log n)^{d+1}/n$ by a factor of $\log n$. A key step is a sharp bracketing bound for multivariate polynomials. For the $L^2(ρ)$ unit ball of real polynomials in $d$ variables with total degree at most $m$, the log bracketing number at width $\varepsilon$ is at most $\binom{m+d}{d}\log(C_d/\varepsilon)$ for $0<\varepsilon\leq1$. The constant $C_d$ depends only on $d$. The bound holds for every positive Borel measure $ρ$ under which each nonzero polynomial in the space has a finite, positive $L^2(ρ)$ norm. We prove the bound using volume estimates for a complex Veronese cone and Gaussian small-ball probabilities, then apply it to bound the local Hellinger bracketing entropy of Gaussian mixture densities. We obtain the matching

candidates.title: Generating health variables for a synthetic population of Santa Catarina, Brazil, via ensemble learning and a calibrated linear program
candidates.abstract: Agent-based models in epidemiology require synthetic populations with health-related attributes, which in Brazil are available only from sample surveys such as the Pesquisa Nacional de Saúde (PNS). We add health variables, including smoking, alcohol consumption, physical exercise, self-rated health and chronic conditions, to a georeferenced synthetic population of the state of Santa Catarina. Class probabilities are estimated by an ensemble of logistic regression, random forest and support vector machine, and individuals are assigned to classes by a linear program that reproduces the class proportions estimated from the survey. We show that, under a mild condition satisfied by our ensemble, the penalty term of this program is no longer needed, and the proportions are reproduced exactly. In a cross-validation on PNS data, the method attains the best results.

candidates.title: A mixed-primal FEM for Poisson-Fermi interfacial problems
candidates.abstract: This paper presents a mixed-primal FEM for a linearised Poisson--Fermi interface problem arising from the Bazant--Storey--Kornyshev theory, which describes electrostatic interactions in ionic solutions. It leads to a transmission problem coupling a fourth-order equation in the solvent region with a second-order equation in the solute region. To precisely compute the electrostatic stress and the interactive force in the electrolyte, we reformulate the fourth-order problem as a mixed system by introducing the gradient of the electrostatic potential, the divergence of its gradient, and the gradient of its divergence as additional independent variables. The second-order problem is studied in its primal form as this approach eliminates the requirement for Lagrange multipliers to enforce the transmission conditions. The resulting formulation is discretised using Raviart--Thomas finite elements for the vector variables and piecewise polynomial finite elements for the scalar variables. Well-posedness of the mixed-primal formulation and optimal a priori error estimates for the field variables as well as for the postprocessed Maxwell tensor are established under suitable regularity assumptio

candidates.title: Combinatorial characterizations of the quantum $\mathfrak{sl}_3$ invariant of positive alternating links and 3-braids
candidates.abstract: The $\mathfrak{sl}_3$ link polynomial is a higher rank relative of the Jones polynomial which can be studied entirely diagrammatically using Kuperberg's web calculus. Building on the work of Harper and Kalfagianni, we construct formulae for the fourth and fifth coefficients of the quantum $\mathfrak{sl}_3$ link invariant on positive alternating link diagrams in terms of data read from the associated Seifert graph. Then, we give a characterization of the invariant on positive alternating fibered links in terms of elementary symmetric polynomials. We also discuss behavior of our formulae under connected sums. We give formulations for the $\mathfrak{sl}_3$ invariant of even powers of the Garside element $Δ_3\in B_3$ and a closed formula for the invariant on positive $3$-braids, resulting in a formula for the invariant on all $3$-braids.

candidates.title: A Sharp Lower Bound for the First Nonzero Steklov Eigenvalue of the Witten Laplacian on Weighted Surfaces with Nonnegative Bakry-Emery-Ricci Tensor
candidates.abstract: We consider compact connected weighted surfaces with smooth boundary whose Bakry-Emery-Ricci tensor is nonnegative. We assume that the geodesic curvature of the boundary is bounded below in terms of the normal and tangential derivatives of the weight function. Under these assumptions, we prove a lower bound for the first nonzero Steklov eigenvalue of the Witten Laplacian, which is sharp in the sense that equality holds if and only if the surface is isometric to a Euclidean disk and the weight function is constant.

candidates.title: The local intertwining relation for inner forms of $\mathrm{GL}_N$
candidates.abstract: The local intertwining relation for inner forms of general linear groups over a local field asserts that the normalized intertwining operator for every parabolically induced representation arising from a local A-parameter is the identity operator. Our main theorem verifies the claim over local fields of characteristic zero. This will serve as a vital ingredient for completing the local intertwining relation and endoscopic classification for non-quasi-split unitary groups.

candidates.title: Generalized Tate--Nakayama duality for complexes of tori over local function fields
candidates.abstract: We define the cohomology set $H^{1}(\mathcal{E}, Z \to T \to U)$ for a complex $Z \to T \to U$ with $T$, $U$ tori over a local function field $F$ and $Z$ a finite subgroup of $T$, where $\mathcal{E}$ is the gerbe from [Dil23]. We follow the method of [Kal26] and prove that the Tate--Nakayama isomorphism [Dil23, Theorem 4.10] for $H^{1}(\mathcal{E}, Z \to T)$ extends to $H^{1}(\mathcal{E}, Z \to T \to U)$, which lets one generalize Kaletha's parametrization [Kal21] of supercuspidal $L$-packets to local function fields.

candidates.title: A Proof of the Ovals Conjecture
candidates.abstract: We prove that the lowest eigenvalue of the periodic Schrödinger operator $-\partial_s^2+κ^2$ on a closed curve of length $\ell$ is at least $4π^2/\ell^2$. Equality holds precisely for the family of ovals described by Benguria and Loss. The proof uses a new comparison argument for scalar ordinary differential equations.

candidates.title: The Residual Unitary Case for Almost Elusive Groups
candidates.abstract: In this short note, we remove the residual unitary family in Hall's classification of almost elusive classical groups and the corresponding conditional family in the quasiprimitive classification. Using theorems of Zsigmondy and Schinzel together with some elementary number theory arguments, we prove that if n > 4 is odd, f > 1 is even, and r is the unique primitive prime divisor of (2^f)^{2n} - 1, then 4nf divides r - 1. For n > 4 prime and any positive integer f, we deduce that a unique primitive prime divisor r of (2^f)^{2n} - 1 satisfies r > 4nf, except when (n, f, r) = (5, 1, 11). We then obtain two conjugacy classes of derangements of the same prime order in a broader family of unitary subspace actions, and a quadratic lower bound for the number of such classes in the corresponding product actions.

candidates.title: Sharp History-Length Dependence of Mesh-Uniform Exponential Decay Rates for a Boundary-Memory Euler-Bernoulli Beam
candidates.abstract: For a boundary-memory Euler--Bernoulli beam with polynomial relaxation, we quantify the loss of exponential stability as the retained history length $S$ grows. The continuous and conforming Hermite--$\mathbb P_1$ generators have zero-frequency resolvent norms bounded above and below by constant multiples of $S$. The bounds are uniform in the beam mesh and in every history mesh of step at most a fixed $h_0$. Their semigroup norms retain a plateau of duration proportional to $S$. Under positive distributed and boundary damping, matching exponential estimates hold with the optimal time scale $1+S$, uniformly in the meshes. Optimality refers to the semigroup norm on the augmented state space, which includes the history. Without distributed damping, the same time scale holds for the continuous truncated generator under a boundary condition on $δ^{(3)}$. We also prove strong convergence of the finite-history semigroups to the full-history semigroup, uniformly on compact time intervals, under restriction and zero extension of histories. candidates.title: Second homotopy modules and infinite homotopy stable classes of four-manifolds
candidates.abstract: We construct infinitely many closed oriented smooth 4-manifolds which are all stably diffeomorphic but pairwise not homotopy equivalent. Our examples are distinguished by their second homotopy modules, and provide the first examples which demonstrate that stable diffeomorphism does not determine the second homotopy module. They have fundamental group $(\mathbb{Z}/4)^4*\mathbb{Z}$ and arise as doubles of presentation 2-complexes. In contrast, we give criteria for isomorphism of second homotopy modules of doubles of 2-complexes, covering finite abelian, quaternion, dihedral and symmetric fundamental groups. We also establish non-injectivity of the doubling construction by showing that there exist homotopically distinct presentation 2-complexes over $Q_{28}$ whose doubles are homotopy equivalent.

candidates.title: Scaling Limits of Time-averaged Distributions for Symmetric Quantum Walks on Hypercubes
candidates.abstract: We study continuous-time and discrete-time quantum walks on the hypercube $\{0,1\}^d$ associated with symmetric random walks, that is, random walks whose transition probabilities depend only on the Hamming distance, using the Hamming scheme and Krawtchouk polynomials. For continuous-time walks, we show that the time-averaged distribution of the Hamming distance is a discrete arcsine law whenever the eigenvalues are distinct. For discrete-time walks, exact formulas for the time-averaged distribution are known as combinatorial sums or as mixtures involving Krawtchouk polynomials, but their scaling limits as $d\to\infty$ (time average first) have not been specified. We obtain them explicitly for three random walks: the simple random walk (an arcsine law), the random walk with binomial weights (an equal mixture of arcsine laws with different supports), and the independent random walk (atoms of mass $1/2$ at $0$ and at $1/2$). Comparing with the continuous-time limits, the two models agree for the simple random walk but differ for the other two, so the correspondence between them is not universal.

candidates.title: Sampling Error in Time-Discretized Stochastic Optimal Control
candidates.abstract: We study sampling error for Euler discretizations of stochastic optimal control problems driven by Brownian motion. For ordinary Monte Carlo sampling, the error can diverge under time refinement when empirical-mean fluctuations accumulate as bias. Under global Lipschitz assumptions and a bounded noise coefficient, we derive finite-sample bounds for the value-function error without assuming smooth value functions or independence across sampling batches. The bounds isolate the empirical-mean contribution. For convergence under time refinement, ordinary Monte Carlo generally requires the number of samples per stage to grow at a faster rate than the number of intervals in the time mesh, whereas antithetic and recentered sampling eliminate the empirical-mean term and yield error bounds uniform over meshes with a fixed sample size per stage. We establish lower bounds showing that the ordinary and antithetic sampling terms are attained. We also prove sample-size convergence for all three methods on fixed meshes. For antithetic and recentered sampling, convergence is uniform over meshes in every noise dimension, with sharp sample-size rates in dimensions at least three.

candidates.title: Realization of expanding dynamics by a finite horizon parabolic law response
candidates.abstract: We study the discrete dynamical system generated by iterating an episodic response of a population density. In each episode, the running potential is frozen at the current density, agents solve a quadratic control problem, and the terminal density is passed to the next episode. For each prescribed positive horizon $τ$ and each $C^k$ map $F$ of finitely many Fourier moments, with $1\le k<\infty$, we construct a finite mode interaction realizing $F$ at order $\varepsilon$. In scaled coordinates, the exact parabolic response satisfies $\|T^{(d)}_{\varepsilon,τ}-(F,S(τ)|_{\Es_d})\|_{C^k}\le C\varepsilon$. The estimate is uniform over a full bounded infinite dimensional Sobolev fibre and needs neither Fourier truncation nor an invariant manifold. For scalar targets with disjoint expanding branches that strictly cover their convex hull, this $C^1$ control and parabolic compactness yield compact invariant sets of the exact response. These sets factor onto the full one sided shift and contain periodic densities of every least period. Nondegenerate periodic orbits continue, and hyperbolicity requires a separate strict multiplier condition. We also prove a derivative cost obstruction for non

candidates.title: Tensor powers of the Steinberg character of $GL_n(\mathbb{F}_q)$, zonotopal algebras, and quiver varieties
candidates.abstract: In this paper we study the $m$-th tensor power ${\rm St}^{\otimes m}$ of the Steinberg character of $GL_n(q)$. To do that we use the connection between tensor products of unipotent characters and the cohomology of certain quiver varieties for star-shaped quivers \cite{L2}\cite{LRV}. We prove that the cohomology ring of the quiver variety associated to ${\rm St}^{\otimes m}$ is generated by its tautological classes. We use this to prove that this cohomology ring is isomorphic to a central zonotopal algebra. We then deduce a combinatorial formula for the multiplicities of unipotent characters in ${\rm St}^{\otimes m}$. This formula has been conjectured by the second author when $m=2$.

candidates.title: An $O(n^{-1/2})$ remainder for the Chow--Robbins stopping boundary
candidates.abstract: We sharpen the asymptotic approximation to the optimal stopping boundary in the Chow--Robbins game, proving the inverse-square-root remainder conjectured by Elton. The proof combines an exactly harmonic integral for simple random walk with a Catalan first-passage renewal identity. Averaging the stopping defect over one spatial period removes its leading lattice dependence, and a coupling of states at equal depth transfers this cancellation to the renewal sum. Consequently, the explicit integer stopping rule can fail at no more than a constant times the square root of the number of observation times.

candidates.title: Adaptive Robust Optimisation for Frequency-Constrained Market Clearing Problem
candidates.abstract: This paper formulates the day-ahead market clearing as a two-stage adaptive robust optimisation problem in which the first stage determines unit commitment, energy dispatch, and reserve procurement, while the second stage represents worst-case balancing actions under simultaneous uncertainty in renewable generation, load, and HVDC converter outages. Frequency security is enforced explicitly through inertia and fast frequency response constraints at the synchronous-area level, with HVDC lines allowed to provide emergency power support within their available headroom. The resulting min--max--min problem is solved by a column-and-constraint generation algorithm and applied to an eight-country North Sea test system comprising three synchronous areas, sixteen onshore bidding zones, and five offshore wind farm hubs connected through a meshed HVDC grid. We compare the Home Market (HM) and Offshore Bidding Zone (OBZ) designs on this infrastructure across different uncertainty scenarios. The results first demonstrate the value of robustness, where deterministic solutions that ignore uncertainty are severely vulnerable to worst-case realisations. Comparing the two designs, we find that OBZ's

candidates.title: On the leading constant in Manin's conjecture
candidates.abstract: We disprove a conjecture of Batyrev and Tschinkel concerning counting rational points of bounded height. Our results strongly suggest that the transcendental Brauer group plays a role in the leading constant in problems of the same nature such as the Manin--Peyre conjecture.

candidates.title: On the unirationality of anticanonical weighted complete intersection surfaces: the infinite families
candidates.abstract: Anticanonical weighted complete intersection surfaces fall into finitely many sporadic families and four infinite families. We prove that the anticanonical surfaces lying in the infinite families are unirational over their field of definition. Over a Hilbertian field, we further prove that a Hilbert subset of members consists of nonrational surfaces.

candidates.title: Flexible algebraic curves and fake vanishing cycles
candidates.abstract: We prove that complex curves in sufficiently ample linear systems on simply connected projective surfaces are topologically (spin) flexible: any (spin) mapping class of the underlying real surface extends to a topological mapping class of the ambient 4-manifold. As a corollary, we prove that smooth curves in the complex projective plane are topologically (spin) flexible. A consequence of topological flexibility is the existence of fake vanishing cycles, that is, simple closed curves on the underlying real surface that are not vanishing cycles, yet still bound a topologically embedded $(\pm1)$-framed disk in the surface exterior. We also give examples of pushed in Seifert surfaces in $D^4$ that are not topologically spin-flexible, but become spin-flexible after a single internal stabilization. Our methods utilize the equivariant intersection form on the surface exterior.

candidates.title: Tube-Based Robust Data-Driven Predictive Control for Linear Parameter-Varying Systems With Noisy Data
candidates.abstract: This paper proposes a tube-based robust data-driven predictive control scheme for unknown discrete-time linear parameter-varying (LPV) systems using offline noisy input-scheduling-state data. We establish a multi-trajectory simplified LPV fundamental lemma yielding a collective Hankel representation of finite-horizon trajectories. Constraining the Hankel coefficients to a scaled simplex uniformly bounds the noise-induced predictor mismatch but may exclude relevant constrained lifted trajectories. A convex-hull coverage condition for admissible receding-horizon continuations restores the required representability. LPV data-consistency and robust positively invariant sets provide tube-tightening ingredients computed directly from noisy data. The online problem is a quadratic program, for which recursive feasibility, closed-loop constraint satisfaction, and practical input-to-state stability are established. Numerical results illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed scheme.

candidates.title: Partition growth homomorphisms on Specht modules
candidates.abstract: There is a unique (up to scalar) representation homomorphism between the Specht modules $\mathcal{S}^λ$ and $\mathcal{S}^μ$ when $μ$ is obtained from $λ$ by adding one to a part of $λ$. We find explicit formulas for these homomorphisms in the Specht polynomial bases of $\mathcal{S}^λ$ and $\mathcal{S}^μ$. Furthermore, given two representation homomorphisms corresponding to adding one to two different parts of $λ$, we find the commutator for the composition of these two homomorphisms. We also extend the Specht polynomial basis of $\mathcal{S}^λ$ into a basis of the permutation module $\mathcal{H}^λ$ and explicitly find a formula for the skew isomorphism from $\mathcal{S}^λ$ to $\mathcal{S}^{λ'}$.

candidates.title: Irrationality and differential equations: the work of Calegari, Dimitrov, and Tang
candidates.comment: Prepared for JMM Current Events Bulletin
candidates.abstract: Beautiful recent work of Calegari, Dimitrov, and Tang has given new methods for proving irrationality of certain arithmetically interesting constants, notably $L(2, χ_{-3})$, building on ideas of Siegel, André, Bost-Charles, and others. This note is meant to explain some of this work for the 2027 JMM Current Events Bulletin, and to situate it in context of some results and conjectures in arithmetic and algebraic geometry.

candidates.title: Dynamical phase transition in Brownian motion via sharp large deviations
candidates.abstract: We prove a dynamical phase transition in Brownian motion with drift, a phenomenon recently predicted in the physics literature. Specifically, when a Brownian motion with drift on a long time interval is conditioned on an upper large deviation event for the (normalized) occupation measure of the interval [-1,1], in the spirit of the Gibbs conditioning principle, a phase transition occurs. If one conditions on a large deviation event in the far upper tail, the conditioned process follows the Langevin diffusion suggested by the Donsker-Varadhan variational formula for additive functionals. In contrast, if one conditions on a large deviation event in the near upper tail, the conditioned process follows a different Langevin diffusion on a fraction of the time interval and subsequently behaves like the unconditioned process. We establish this phase transition via a new sharp large deviation result for the occupation measure, which is of independent interest. We also provide further corollaries of this result and discuss generalizations to other Markov processes and additive functionals.

candidates.title: Sub-Riemannian Distances on Lie Groups: Tangent Asymptotics and Hermitian Matrix Formulas
candidates.abstract: Let $d_{\mathrm{SR}}$ be the Carnot--Carathéodory distance associated with a two-step Lie pair and let $d_0$ be the distance on its nilpotent tangent group. For compact Lie pairs we prove, locally uniformly in $(X,Z)$, \[ d_{\mathrm{SR}}\!\left(e,\exp(rX+r^2Z)\right)^2 =r^2d_0(e,(X,Z))^2+O(r^3). \] For symmetric pairs, the remainder improves to $O(r^4)$. This order is sharp in general, and the estimate remains uniform at cut points, abnormal endpoints, and points where the tangent endpoint map changes rank. If the tangent minimizer is unique, the endpoint differential is onto, and the constrained Hessian is coercive, we determine the coefficient of $r^4$ with remainder $O(r^6)$. For block subgroups of $\mathrm{SU}(N)$, we express the vertical squared distance on the tangent group as the attained minimum of a finite-dimensional functional on Hermitian matrices subject to linear constraints on their partial traces. Every minimizer gives a minimizing loop represented by a trigonometric polynomial. For one $m$-dimensional block and $q$ scalar blocks, the coefficient has weights $\lceil j/q\rceil$ and reduces to a trace norm formula when $q\ge\lfloor m/2\rfloor$.

candidates.title: Quantum Control Under Control-Dependent Decoherence
candidates.abstract: Decoherence, which arises from the interaction of a quantum system with a typically much larger thermal environment, or bath, poses major challenges to the controllability of quantum systems. The dynamics of such open quantum systems is often represented by Markovian quantum master equations of the Lindblad or Redfield type. These equations describe the dynamics of the open system with a sum of coherent (Hamiltonian) and decoherent (dissipative) contributions. It is often assumed that coherent controls only impact the coherent contribution, while the decoherent contribution is taken to be time- and control-independent. However, the decoherent contribution must also be control-dependent if coupling to a thermal bath is to relax the system to a Gibbs state at thermal equilibrium, which is given in terms of the system's Hamiltonian. In this paper, we investigate the effect of accounting for control-dependent decoherence on coherent control protocols. To this end, we examine the effect of accounting for control-dependent decoherence on the controllability of an open quantum system in the case of a two-level system coupled to a thermal bath. We show that coherent controls wield greater

candidates.title: Cycle popping and positivity in linear Laurent phenomenon algebras
candidates.abstract: We prove that every monomial in the cluster variables of a linear Laurent phenomenon algebra is a nonnegative combination of cluster monomials, as conjectured by Lam and the second author. The proof uses Wilson's cycle popping. We also give a new proof of Laurent positivity in linear Laurent phenomenon algebras, previously established by the first author.

candidates.title: Which Ellipses Are Outlines of a Given Ellipsoid? A Ratio Test with Unknown Focal Length
candidates.comment: 36 pages, 6 figures, 4 tables; supplementary material included as an ancillary file. Submitted to SIAM Journal on Imaging Sciences. Code: https://github.com/michael-werman/realizability-code
candidates.abstract: When is an image ellipse the outline of a given ellipsoid with semi-axes $a <= b <= c? For a camera with square pixels, zero skew and known principal point, we show that it is an outline at focal length $f$ exactly when a cone ratio kappa(f), computed from two eigenvalues, is at most a/c; the middle semi-axis b plays no role. With f unknown, the admissible focal lengths form an interval; whether it is empty is decided by the smallest cone ratio over $f$, which, when attained, is obtained from an explicit quartic. The interval is bounded above only when the principal point is closer to the long axis of the ellipse than to its short axis. Thus one ellipse can rule out ellipsoids that are too round, never ones that are too elongated, and none if the principal point is unknown. Simulations and 45 Cassini images of Saturn's moons support the test.

candidates.title: Disjointness, Orthogonality and Commutativity in $C^*$-Algebras
candidates.abstract: We characterize order-theoretic disjointness of two elements $a$ and $b$ in the self-adjoint part of a $C^*$-algebra $A$ via the condition $aAb = \{0\}$ and the trivial intersection of closed two-sided ideals generated by $a$ and $b$. As a consequence, we show that disjoint complements coincide with the self-adjoint parts of annihilator ideals. We also prove that $A$ is commutative whenever every pair of algebraically orthogonal positive contractions in $A$ is disjoint. Finally, we establish corresponding commutativity criteria involving projections for real rank zero $C^*$-algebras.

candidates.title: Fake surfaces for some potential Andrews-Curtis counterexamples
candidates.abstract: Andrews and Curtis famously conjectured that every contractible $2$-complex $3$-deforms to a point and, in fact, it suffices to consider contractible closed fake surfaces. The traditional potential counterexamples are given as balanced presentations of the trivial group. In this article, we construct closed fake surfaces for the Akbulut-Kirby family of potential counterexamples using geodesic loops in a metric classifying space for the $3$-strand braid group. Concretely we construct a $(2n+1)$-vertex fake surface for $\mathrm{AK}_n$ with a cyclically symmetric $1$-skeleton. Our $7$-vertex fake surface for $\mathrm{AK}_3$ is the simplest fake surface whose Andrews-Curtis status is unknown.

candidates.title: RSK with a twist, mirabolic Steinberg variety, and Pak--Postnikov representations
candidates.abstract: There is a beautiful interplay between the classical Robinson--Schensted correspondence and the Steinberg variety, which is the union of conormal components of $Fl(V) \times Fl(V)$. The irreducible components of the Steinberg variety gives the geometric interpretation of RS, and Pak--Postnikov description of RS as U,D operators is the combinatorics shadow of the $S_n\times S_n$-representation inside the top homology of the Steinberg variety. We study the conormal components of $Fl(V) \times Fl(V) \times L(λ)$, where $L(λ)$ is an irreducible representation of $GL(V)$. We show that there are only three families of $L(λ)$ such that $Fl(V)\times Fl(V) \times L(λ)$ has finitely many orbits. These families are determinant twists of classical RS, Travkin's mirabolic RSK and its Fourier dual. We extend the combinatorial interpretation of RS in terms of U,D operators to mirabolic RSK. Finally, we give a filtration of the top homology of the mirabolic Steinberg variety in which each graded piece is a Pak--Postnikov $S_n \times S_n$-representations.

candidates.title: Supercuspidal representations and types via double covers and the Fourier--Weil representation
candidates.abstract: We present a construction of supercuspidal representations and types for tame $p$-adic groups whose input is a generic essentially depth-zero representation of a double covers of twisted Levi subgroups. This clarifies and simplifies existing constructions by automatically producing and explaining the twisting quadratic character of Fintzen--Kaletha--Spice, the roots of unity in the Harish-Chandra character formula, and making the connection to the Galois side of the local Langlands correspondence immediate. The main innovation is the use of a Fourier model of the Weil representation defined on an extension of the symplectic group by the Witt group.

candidates.title: Notes for a seminar on vortex layer cascades
candidates.abstract: After the seminars I recently gave at New York University, the University of Chicago, Princeton University and the University of Bonn and after having been asked by some people to publish these notes, I decided to upload them to arXiv. In recent years, the method of vortex layer cascades has successfully been applied to construct finite-time singularities in multiple fluid equations (3D Euler, Boussinesq, IPM, g-SQG...). In this talk, I will motivate and describe the method and sketch how it can be applied to the 2D Boussinesq and 2D non-homogeneous Euler equations. In both systems, the growth of the vorticity is driven by an accumulated hysteresis effect triggered by the cyclic deformation of the density layers, whose dynamics is governed by an infinite chain of degenerate pendula. Our work also settles the previously open question about global existence of classical solutions of the (forced) 2D non-homogeneous Euler equations.

candidates.title: Smyth completeness and nonexpansive iteration in $q$-hyperconvex $T_0$-quasi-metric spaces
candidates.abstract: We study the specialization order $\le_d$, defined by $x\le_d y$ if and only if $d(x,y)=0$, of a $q$-hyperconvex $T_0$-quasi-metric space $(X,d)$. We show that every nonempty bounded subset $A$ of $X$ has an infimum $\bigwedge A$ characterized by the metric formula $d(w,\bigwedge A)=\sup_{a\in A}d(w,a)$ for all $w\in X$, and dually a supremum, and that powers and copowers exist. For bounded $X$ this gives an elementary proof, with explicit metric formulas, of the known fact that Isbell-convex Lawvere metric spaces are complete in the sense of enriched category theory; the formulas themselves and the extension to bounded subsets of unbounded $q$-hyperconvex spaces are not covered by the enriched-categorical argument, which requires radii in $[0,\infty]$. Consequently no $T_1$-quasi-metric space with at least two points is $q$-hyperconvex, and the fixed points of every order-preserving self-map of a bounded $q$-hyperconvex space form a nonempty complete lattice. We show that the fixed point set of a nonexpansive self-map need not be a sublattice and that the specialization order need not be distributive. Our main result concerns the continuity of nonexpansive maps. Nonexpansive self-

candidates.title: Time-uniform bounds and long-time asymptotics for a three-species drift-diffusion model for memristors
candidates.abstract: The qualitative behavior of weak solutions to the two-dimensional drift-diffusion equations for memristors, incorporating Shockley-Read-Hall-type generation-recombination terms and time-dependent boundary conditions, is investigated. The model couples the electron, hole, and oxygen-vacancy densities to the electric potential through the Poisson equation. The global existence and uniqueness of weak solutions are established. If the boundary data converge to the thermal equilibrium at an integrable rate, the densities remain uniformly-in-time bounded above and below, and the solution converges exponentially fast to thermal equilibrium. For time-independent boundary data and sufficiently small applied bias, solutions converge exponentially fast to steady states carrying nonzero fluxes.

candidates.title: On the number of positive solutions of the nonlinear Schrödinger equation on compact star graphs
candidates.abstract: In this paper, we consider the number and the shape of positive solutions of the nonlinear Schrödinger equation on compact symmetric star graphs with Dirichlet condition at the exterior vertex and Kirchhoff condition at the central vertex.

candidates.title: Explicit KL Exponents for PLQ Functions on the Sphere
candidates.abstract: Let $φ$ be a proper piecewise linear-quadratic (PLQ) function whose domain meets the unit sphere $\mathcal{S}$. We prove that $f:=φ+δ_{\mathcal{S}}$, where $δ_{\mathcal{S}}$ is the indicator function of $\mathcal{S}$, satisfies the Kurdyka--Łojasiewicz (KL) property with exponent $3/4$ throughout its domain. This exponent is sharp even for the convex PLQ class. We characterize the smallest KL exponents of quadratics restricted to affine sections of $\mathcal{S}$, obtaining the values $0$, $1/2$, $2/3$, and $3/4$. A tangential projection identity shows that, at each point of ${\rm dom}\,f$, the maximum of the exponents from the relevant affine sections is admissible for $f$. When $φ$ is piecewise affine (PA), each of these smallest exponents is $0$ or $1/2$. Thus $f$ satisfies the KL property with exponent $1/2$ throughout ${\rm dom}\,f$, and this exponent is sharp over the class of sphere-constrained PA functions. When ${\rm dom}\,φ$ is a finite union of closed polyhedral cones, $f$ admits KL exponent $1/2$ for homogeneous quadratic pieces and exponent $0$ for nonnegative $φ$ that is linear on each cone. For any convex polytope $C$ containing the origin, we use the KL exponent $0$

candidates.title: Similarity classes of $5\times5$ matrices over local rings of length two
candidates.abstract: Let $R$ be a commutative local principal ideal ring of length two whose residue field has arbitrary characteristic. Prasad, Singla and Spallone classified similarity classes in $M_n(R)$ for $n\leq4$ by using module extensions. We extend their classification to $n=5$. We determine explicit extension-orbit representatives and stabilizers for the partitions $(3,2)$, $(2,2,1)$ and $(2,1,1,1)$. We prove that every orbit contains exactly one of the listed representatives. Together with the known primary cases, these results give all similarity classes in $M_5(R)$ and their centralizers. We also determine representatives and stabilizers for the family $(m+1,1,1,1)$ for every $m\geq1$. When the residue field is finite, we obtain the sizes and total number of similarity classes.

candidates.title: A proof of the toughness conjecture for Kneser graphs
candidates.abstract: As a measure of the connectivity of graphs, Chvátal \cite{Chvatal} introduced the concept of toughness. For integers $k\geq2$ and $n\geq2k+1$, the Kneser graph $\KG(n,k)$ has all the $k$-subsets of $[n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}$ as its vertices, and two vertices are adjacent if they are disjoint. Cioabă and Wong~\cite{CW} determined the toughness of $\KG(n,2)$. Park et al.~\cite{Park} determined the toughness of $\KG(n,k)$ when $k=3,4$ and $k\geq5$ for large $n$. They \cite{Park} proposed a conjecture for $k\geq5$ and other values of $n$. In this paper, we resolve this conjecture.

candidates.title: The pair correlation of $αn+β\log n$ modulo one
candidates.abstract: We show that for any non-Liouville irrational $α$ and for any real $β\ne0$, the sequence $\left(αn+β\log n\right)_{n=1}^{\infty}$ has Poissonian pair correlation modulo one.

candidates.title: On local embeddability into $C^*(\F_\infty)$
candidates.abstract: We study local embeddability of $C^*$-algebras into $C^*(\F_\infty)$ as an analogue of QWEP in the LLP/WEP picture. We characterize this property by an analog of CP-stability, an approximation property for finite-dimensional operator systems. We show that local embeddability, together with an amenable trace, implies a tracial local lifting property. Combining this observation with the cohomological obstructions of Ioana, Spaas and Wiersma, we prove that the full group $C^*$-algebra $C^*(\SL_3(\Z))$ does not locally embed into $C^*(\F_\infty)$. We obtain the same conclusion for the full $C^*$-algebras of two hyperlinear groups constructed by Thom. To our knowledge, the only previously known obstruction to local embeddability into $C^*(\F_\infty)$ was due to Junge and Pisier.

candidates.title: Boundedness and Kawamata-Viehweg vanishing for threefolds of Fano type in large characteristics
candidates.abstract: We study threefolds over algebraically closed fields of large positive characteristic. Let \((X,B)\) be a projective log canonical pair with \(X\) of Fano type, \(-(K_X+B)\) nef and coefficients of \(B\) in a fixed hyperstandard set. We obtain a monotonic complement of bounded index. For exceptional pairs the complement is Kawamata log terminal. We prove that all \(ε\)-log canonical weak log Fano threefolds are arithmetically bounded above a characteristic threshold independent of \(ε\). We also prove Kawamata--Viehweg vanishing for integral \(\Q\)-Cartier Weil divisors on projective threefolds of Fano type above an absolute characteristic threshold.

candidates.title: The first moment of symmetric cube $L$-functions
candidates.abstract: We establish a power saving asymptotic formula for the first moment of symmetric cube central $L$-values over Hecke--Maass forms in short spectral windows. As applications, we prove quantitative non-vanishing, an almost-all Lindelöf bound, and almost-all decay of cubic periods. We also prove the corresponding first moment asymptotic for central derivatives in the holomorphic weight aspect. Our proof begins with an application of the Kuznetsov formula, followed by a first Poisson summation and stationary phase analysis. The key observation is that a periodic cubic factor can be separated from the resulting oscillation and incorporated into the arithmetic sum, allowing a second application of Poisson summation to yield further cancellation.

candidates.title: Exact Solutions and a Critical-Damping Threshold for a Nonlinear Transport-Wave Equation
candidates.abstract: Linear stability theory does not determine whether a small disturbance in a physical system decays or grows without bound when the disturbance has finite size and the damping varies in time. We address this question for the nonlinear damped transport-wave equation $u_{tt}+cu_{xt}+γu_t=λu(u_t+cu_x)e^{-γt}$, a constant-coefficient case of a model introduced in previous work. Combining the method of characteristics with a Riccati reduction, we reduce the equation exactly to a first-order ordinary differential equation at each point and solve it explicitly. For a natural class of initial data, the solution has a critical damping rate $\gc$, given in closed form in terms of the initial data: for $γ<\gc$ the solution blows up in finite time, and otherwise no finite-time singularity occurs. A similar result holds for time-dependent damping and for power-law feedback. Applications to shock formation in the damped Burgers equation, gelation with decaying reactivity and frictional heating under a moving band are presented.

candidates.title: From Horner's rule to neural networks
candidates.abstract: Horner's rule is usually taught as an efficient algorithm for evaluating a polynomial. Read as a recurrence, however, it is also a small computational graph: an input is propagated through intermediate states, while parameters enter locally. This note follows that elementary observation from polynomial evaluation to polynomial fitting. The equation $Va\simeq y$ then unifies least-squares approximation, interpolation and overparametrisation as different regimes of a fixed representation. Neural networks are introduced as the next step: the representation itself becomes parametrised and is learned from data. The purpose is pedagogical rather than encyclopaedic. It offers a numerical route into machine learning, using approximation, linear algebra and optimisation as familiar entry points.

candidates.title: $L^p$-boundedness of magnetic pseudodifferential operators
candidates.abstract: We show that $L^p$-boundedness for magnetic pseudodifferential operators is equivalent to $L^p$-boundedness of non-magnetic pseudodifferential operators for $p\in[1,\infty]$, regular magnetic fields and classical Hörmander symbols $S_{ρ,δ}^m$ with $0<ρ\leq 1$ and $0\leqδ<1$. As a corollary we get $L^p$-boundedness for $1<p<\infty$ of magnetic pseudodifferential operators when $ρ>0,0\leqδ\leqρ\leq1,δ<1$ and $m\leq-d(1-ρ)|1/2-1/p|$. Moreover, we give a bound on the operator norm in terms of the magnetic field and symbol.

candidates.title: The Orientable Genus of Generalized Corona Graphs
candidates.abstract: The generalized corona of a graph with a family of graphs, one for each vertex, is obtained by joining every vertex of the base graph to all vertices of its own copy of the corresponding graph; the corona of Frucht and Harary is the case in which all graphs in the family are equal. Each attached copy meets the rest of the graph in a single vertex, so additivity of the orientable genus over blocks reduces the genus of a generalized corona to the genus of the base graph plus the genera of the graphs obtained from the attached graphs by adding a dominating vertex. We study this last quantity through faces that meet every vertex, and we determine it for complete graphs, balanced complete bipartite graphs, wheels, prisms, antiprisms, the Petersen graph (value 2). The Petersen case follows from a face-length criterion. We also obtain bounds under edge addition, a formula for iterated coronas, a criterion for two coronas taken in opposite order to have the same genus, and we show that the corona is not associative with respect to the genus.

candidates.title: Characteristic-Free Skew-Symmetric Classical Invariant Theor
candidates.abstract: We study an exterior-algebra analogue of classical invariant theory for linear, symplectic, and orthogonal groups, with particular emphasis on integral constructions and positive characteristic. The theory presented here is rather different from the classical one developed by us in DeConcini Procesi 1976 . In fact, the present theory is based on good filtrations and on a surprising divided-power structure on the algebras of exterior invariants. We also include a short characteristic-zero treatment of the corresponding First and Second Fundamental Theorems via the exterior Cauchy identity; these known results motivate the integral theory.

candidates.title: Convergence and error analysis of problem-independent machine learning (PIML) with linear completeness
candidates.abstract: Problem-independent machine learning (PIML) is an effective computational approach that combines the finite element method with machine learning. PIML uses neural networks to learn the mapping from material distributions or element geometries to the numerical shape functions of substructures. This approach avoids repeated computation while preserving the conformity of the underlying finite element discretization, thereby significantly improving the efficiency of substructure-based finite element analysis. However, existing studies on PIML have primarily focused on numerical accuracy and computational efficiency, while rigorous theoretical analyses of its approximation errors are still limited. In this paper, we establish an error analysis framework for PIML from a classical finite element perspective, in which the numerical error is bounded in terms of the finite element discretization error and the network generalization error. Our analysis shows that, when only rigid-body displacement invariance is enforced, the resulting error estimate contains a learning-induced term that does not necessarily decrease under mesh refinement. To ensure convergence, we propose an improved PIML sch

candidates.title: Harmonic multi-valued $1$-forms and deformations of branched covers of special Lagrangians
candidates.abstract: This article introduces the notion of a non-degenerate multi-valued $1$-form on a manifold $X$ in terms of immersed submanifolds of $T^*X$ and develops a deformation theory extending Donaldson's work on harmonic non-degenerate $\mathbf{Z}/2\mathbf{Z}$ $1$-forms. More precisely, the universal moduli space of harmonic non-degenerate multi-valued $1$-forms is shown to be a tame Fréchet orbifold whose projection onto the space of Riemannian metrics is a submersion and whose fibres are locally parametrised by their periods. The proof relies on Hörmander's subelliptic estimates and the Nash--Moser submersion theorem. As an application of this analytic framework, harmonic multi-valued $1$-forms on a special Lagrangian are shown to control deformations of its branched covers, extending work of He for multiplicity two.

candidates.title: Weak oddness to resistance ratios in snarks
candidates.abstract: Let $G$ be a bridgeless cubic graph. If $G$ is not 3-edge-colourable, we call it a \textit{snark}. The \textit{resistance} of $G$, denoted $r(G)$, is the minimum number of edges which can be removed from $G$ in order to render $G$ 3-edge-colourable. The \textit{oddness} of $G$, denoted $ω(G)$, is the minimum number of odd components in any 2-factor of $G$. The \textit{weak oddness} of $G$, denoted $ω'(G)$, is the minimum number of odd components in any even factor of $G$. In their comprehensive survey paper on measurements of uncolourability in cubic graphs, Fiol et al. conjectured the following two statements for a snark $G$: $ω(G) \leq 2r(G)$ and $ω'(G) \leq 2r(G)$ \cite{FiolMazzuoccoloSteffen2018}. Previously, we disproved the former by proving that the ratio of oddness to weak oddness, and hence the ratio of oddness to resistance, can in fact be arbitrarily large \cite{Allie2019}. In this paper, we prove a slightly stronger version of the latter: $ω'(G) < 2r(G)$. The proof centres around substructures in $G$, given a minimal colouring $f$, which we call \textit{meta-Kempe chains}.

candidates.title: Commutator syzygies and pure resolutions over central polynomial rings with division-ring coefficients
candidates.abstract: Let $D$ be a division ring and let $A=D[x,y,z]$ with central indeterminates. For positive integers $p,q$ and $a,b\in D$, put $f=x^p+az^p$ and $g=y^q+bz^q$. We compute their left syzygy module and the minimal graded free resolution of $A/(Af+Ag)$. This quotient has projective dimension two if $ab=ba$ and three otherwise. In the latter case, it has finite length and total Betti numbers $(1,2,2,1)$, with a pure resolution of type $(0,d,3d,4d)$ when $p=q=d$. These tables do not occur over polynomial rings over fields. If $D$ is finite-dimensional over its center $K$, the Betti tables of modules of finite length over $K[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ and left modules of finite length over $D[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ generate the same rational cone for every $n\ge1$. In three variables, the semigroup over $K$ is properly contained in that over $D$ when $D$ is noncommutative.

candidates.title: Semirings Induced by Semilattices
candidates.abstract: We investigate semirings induced by join-semilattice (meet-semilattices) with a degenerate multiplication on all the subset that excludes the multiplicative unity. The way those semirings are defined enables a big impact of the semilattices we start with on the associated semirings: many of their order-theoretic properties reflect in algebraic properties of the induced semirings. This enabled constructing examples of semirings with desired properties as well as providing counterexamples to wrong claims in old and recent papers/preprints. In particular, we construct families of examples of semirings induced by non-modular join-semilattices for which the lattice of subtractive ideals is non-modular disproving a claim of Henriksen who introduced this important class of ideals of semirings.

candidates.title: Certified minimax normal-scale mixtures for the logistic-normal integral
candidates.abstract: The logistic distribution function is a scale mixture of normal distribution functions, and Monahan and Stefanski approximate it by the $K$-term mixture $Λ(x) \approx \sum_{i} w_i Φ(s_i x)$ chosen to minimise the uniform error on the real line. Each such mixture reduces the logistic-normal integral to a sum of $K$ normal distribution functions with the mixture's uniform error bound. This integral is the expectation of a logistic sigmoid over a normal distribution in statistics and the Gauss-Fermi integral in semiconductor physics. Monahan and Stefanski tabulate constants for $K \le 8$ and conjecture that the optimal error equioscillates at $2K$ points, while above $K = 8$ the Remez exchange and local solvers stall at nonequioscillating stationary points. We prove that the tangent space of the mixture family is a Chebyshev system, which forces $2K$-point equioscillation at every interior minimiser and makes any such solution the unique global minimax, and we prove interior attainment for $K \le 11$. A certification algorithm audits a candidate mixture in multiple-precision arithmetic, using a proved bound on the number of extrema as its completeness test, and three search pipelines

candidates.title: Linear convergence of evolution strategies to local minima by coupling with quadratic models
candidates.abstract: Among derivative-free optimization methods, evolution strategies have emerged as competitive algorithms for multimodal, noisy or ill-conditioned problems in small and moderate dimensions. Theoretical guarantees have long been scarce, but a series of recent works established their convergence on certain classes of objective functions. A successful approach normalizes the states of the algorithm into a Markov chain and proves that this chain converges to a stationary distribution. It has yielded the linear convergence of several evolution strategies, including the state-of-the-art CMA-ES. Yet this approach requires the objective function to be scaling-invariant, hence unimodal, since otherwise the normalized process is not a Markov chain. We propose a methodology to prove linear convergence on a much larger class of functions, including smooth multimodal functions. Started close enough to a local minimum with a nondegenerate Hessian and with a small enough step size, the ($μ$/$μ$w, $λ$)-ES with stepsize adaptation converges linearly to this minimum with high probability, at the rate of its quadratic model, and the probability of failure vanishes when the initial step size and the ini

candidates.title: The Commutant of the Adjoint Center Need Not Be the Center of the Dual
candidates.abstract: Let $X$ be a Banach lattice with ideal center $Z(X)$, and let $Z^*(X)=\{S^*:S\in Z(X)\}$ be the set of adjoints of central operators, acting on the dual $X^*$. The center $Z(X^*)$ of the dual is always contained in the commutant $(Z^*(X))^{\mathrm{com}}$ of $Z^*(X)$, and equality is known when $X$ has a topological order unit. It has been asserted that equality holds whenever $X$ has a topologically full center; the published proof of this assertion is incorrect, and the question has been recorded as open. We show that the assertion is false. candidates.title: Minkowski problems for $(s,q)$-chord measures
candidates.abstract: Motivated by the work of Lutwak--Xi--Yang--Zhang on the chord measures, we introduce the $(s,q)$-chord measures arising from variations of a new family of geometric invariants, called the $(s,q)$-chord integrals. When $s=1$, the $(s,q)$-chord measures recover the chord measures. We study the corresponding Minkowski problems for the \((s,q)\)-chord measure.

candidates.title: Magnetic vector fields with isolated singularities
candidates.abstract: We construct unit-length, divergence-free vector fields tangent to the boundary on arbitrary smoothly bounded domains in $\mathbb R^3$. These vector fields are continuously differentiable except for a finite number of points on the boundary. Our approach identifies a form of h-principle and a close analogy with Nash's construction of smooth isometric embeddings.

candidates.title: Observable sets for one-dimensional Schrödinger equations with subquadratic power potentials
candidates.abstract: In this paper, we study observability inequalities for the one-dimensional Schrödinger equation associated with the operator $H_m=-\partial_x^2+|x|^{2m}$, where $0<m\leq1$. For $0<m<1/2$, observability in some positive time, and equivalently in every positive time, is characterized by the thickness of the observation set. This extends the characterization of Chen--Liu--Liu at $m=1/2$. For $1/2<m\leq1$, we characterize observable sets in terms of the asymptotic lower density on the spatial intervals $I_{m,a}(x)=[x-a|x|^{2m-1},x+a|x|^{2m-1}]$. Observability in some positive time is equivalent to positive density at some scale, whereas observability in every positive time is equivalent to positive density at every scale. Moreover, for $1/2<m<1$, the minimal observation time is comparable to the square root of the critical density scale.

candidates.title: An improved estimate for discrete $L^8$ restriction on the cubic curve
candidates.abstract: We prove an improved estimate for discrete $L^8$ restriction on the cubic curve $(n,n^3)$. candidates.title: Some conservativity results for weak arithmetic theories in a language with exponentiation
candidates.abstract: Recall that $\mathsf{IOpen}$ denotes the theory of quantifier-free induction in the pure arithmetic language. In this paper, we consider an extension of $\mathsf{IOpen}$ in the arithmetical language expanded by the unary function $\exp: x \mapsto 2^x$, obtained by adding certain simple universal axioms for $\exp$, namely, $$\exp(1) = 2, \quad \exp(x + y) = \exp(x) \exp(y), \quad \exp(x) > x.$$ We prove that this theory is $Π_1$-conservative over $\mathsf{IOpen}$ and $\forall$-conservative over the theory of discretely ordered $\mathbb Z$-semirings. This result extends a result of A. Wilkie and provides a partial answer to a question of E. Jeřábek concerning the strength of the theory of exponential integer parts.

candidates.title: Spectrality of additive measures with Bernoulli convolutions
candidates.abstract: The spectral properties of additive measures of Lebesgue type are by now completely settled \cite{LLP21,ALZ23,KW25,Lu25}. In this paper we continue the study of spectrality for Cantor-type additive measures. For $0<r<1$, let $μ_r$ denote the Bernoulli convolution generated by the maps $x\mapsto rx$ and $x\mapsto r(x+2)$ with equal weights, and consider the Bernoulli-type additive measure \[ μ_{r,s}=\tfrac12(μ_r\timesδ_0+δ_0\timesμ_s). \] For every even integer $R=2k$ we construct an explicit spectrum of the one-dimensional measure $μ_{1/R}$, and from it an explicit spectrum of $μ^{1/R}:=μ_{1/R,1/R}$ lying on the antidiagonal is constructed. Combined with the recently established absence of Fourier frames for the Bernoulli convolutions $μ_{1/N}$ for odd integers $N\geq3$ \cite{DLT26,FSW26}, this yields a parity dichotomy: $μ^{1/R}$ is spectral if and only if $R$ is even. For unequal contraction ratios, we prove that $μ_{1/2,1/4}$ is not spectral. Several open problems and future directions are discussed.

candidates.title: Gaps between zeros of Epstein zeta-functions of binary quadratic forms on the critical line
candidates.abstract: We prove that for every integral binary quadratic form $Q$ whose discriminant is, up to sign, not a perfect square, the Epstein zeta-function of $Q$ has a zero $\frac12+iγ$ with $|γ-T|\le T^{2/5+ε}$ for all large $T$. For indefinite $Q$, that is, for zeta-functions of ideal classes of real quadratic orders, this is the first exponent below the classical barrier $1/2$. For positive definite $Q$ it improves the exponents $5/11$ of Jutila and Srinivas and $3/7$ of the authors, and for discriminant $-4m^2$ with $m$ odd we obtain $1/3$. A main ingredient, of independent interest, is an explicit Voronoi summation formula with additive twists to every modulus for the representation numbers of an indefinite binary form. The resulting dual sums are treated by a two-dimensional Weyl differencing, controlled by an exact formula for the Hessian determinant of the differenced phase.

candidates.title: The optimal exponent in the Babai-Goodman-Pyber theorem
candidates.abstract: Babai, Goodman and Pyber proved that there exists an absolute constant $c$ such that $[X:\operatorname{Rad}(X)]\le [X:H]^c$ for every finite group $X$ and every soluble subgroup $H\le X$, where $\operatorname{Rad}(X)$ denotes the largest soluble normal subgroup of $X$. We prove that the least possible value of $c$ is $b_0=1+\log_9(168\cdot 24^{1/3})\approx3.8141$. For nonsoluble $X$, we obtain the stronger inequality $[X:\operatorname{Rad}(X)]\le 24^{-1/3}[X:H]^{b_0}$, and the coefficient $24^{-1/3}$ is optimal for this exponent. We reduce the problem to bounds on soluble subgroups of automorphism groups of finite simple groups. Examples based on $\operatorname{PSL}_2(8)$ establish sharpness.
